_meta.description: VANILLA Morrowind in-game literature index: every book, note, scroll, and letter with meaningful text (449 distinct texts from the Morrowind/Tribunal/Bloodmoon ESMs), summarized in ORIGINAL WORDS for lore reference and discussion. This file is vanilla-only — NP-server lore lives in lore.json.

conventions.ip: Summaries are freshly written; the KB never contains or reproduces in-game book text. If a user asks for a book's full text, say the codex holds summaries only and point them to the book in-game. Never quote passages, verse lines, or refrains — titles and proper nouns only.
conventions.voice: In-world books are written by in-world authors with agendas — Temple doctrine, Imperial scholarship, Ashlander tradition, satire, and outright self-mythology (the 36 Lessons of Vivec are Vivec's own esoteric self-account, not history). Weigh a book's type and origin before treating its claims as fact.
conventions.vanilla_only_answering: Answer vanilla lore from this file and vanilla_lore.json — never from the internet. Refer to UESP only for what these files do not cover (quest walkthroughs, NPC dialogue, locations).

s-esm.note: Book records parsed from local Morrowind/Tribunal/Bloodmoon ESMs; summaries derived from those texts (original wording).

books.title: 2920, Evening Star
books.summary: Almalexia recovers from a long illness and urges Vivec to leave her side and finally sign the long-delayed peace treaty with Emperor Reman III in the Imperial City. There the Morag Tong assassin Corda, sent by Potentate Versidue-Shaie and avenging her executed sister, kills Reman III with a concealed blade, after which the Potentate quietly seizes control, declines the title of Emperor, and proclaims the start of the Second Era. In a closing scene, Sotha Sil's vast clockwork mechanism beneath Ebonheart suffers a small, irreversible malfunction that he recognizes as unfixable and momentous.

books.title: 2920, First Seed
books.summary: This installment of the 2920 chronicle follows Emperor Reman III, persuaded by the Akaviri Potentate Versidue-Shaie to stay out of the vanguard, while a Breton double agent feeds Vivec's forces intelligence on the Imperial battle order. Vivec lures the exhausted Imperial army into a flooded, spear-choked river crossing near Bodrum by damming the water and drilling his soldiers in crafting simple wooden spears, resulting in a devastating ambush that annihilates the vanguard and much of the flanking forces.

books.title: 2920, FrostFall
books.summary: In High Rock, the young Dunmer witch Turala quickly masters conjuration under coven leader Mynistera and travels to Wayrest with two coven sisters, leaving behind her infant daughter Bosriel. Meanwhile her former lover Cassyr Whitley, publicly humiliated by tales of his botched spy work for Vivec during the war, seeks out the coven hoping to curse the living god, learning from an expelled Psijic that only witches and Psijics may summon daedra during wartime. Returning to find the coven burned and Bosriel missing after an orc raid, Cassyr falsely tells the grieving Turala that agents of the Duke of Mournhold are responsible, deliberately steering her rage toward Morrowind.

books.title: 2920, Hearth Fire
books.summary: The ninth installment of the serialized novel 2920, set in the final year of the First Era, intercutting several storylines: Empress Tavia's grief-stricken secret escape from Castle Giovese with help from her retainer Zuuk; Emperor Reman III and the Potentate Versidue-Shaie orchestrating the execution of Lady Rijja for the assassination of the Imperial Prince; and the Dunmer spy Cassyr Athram fleeing High Rock with Turala and her infant Bosriel, who are saved from an orc hunting party by the witch Mynista Skeffington, who explains conjuration as building friendly relationships with spirits rather than commanding them.

books.title: 2920, Last Seed
books.summary: In this installment of the 2920 series, Prince Juilek Cyrodiil negotiates and signs a peace treaty with Vivec, Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and the Duke of Mournhold at Ald Lambasi, ending the long war between Cyrodiil and Morrowind. Riding on to his imprisoned mother's aid in Black Marsh, Juilek is ambushed and killed by a mercenary named Miramor, hired by an unseen employer to destroy incriminating correspondence; Miramor burns the letter but keeps the signed treaty. A parallel thread follows Cassyr Whitley, a deserter sympathetic to Morrowind, who befriends an exiled Dunmer woman, Turala, and her newborn daughter while fleeing toward High Rock.

books.title: 2920, MidYear
books.summary: Dated chronicle entries follow Vivec's forces preparing to defend the fortresses Ald Iuval and Ald Marak against an advancing Imperial army in the year 2920. Vivec's spy misjudges enemy battlemages as mere healers, allowing Prince Juilek's heavily armored troops to cross Lake Coronati underwater via a water-breathing spell and seize Ald Marak by surprise. Potentate Versidue-Shaie claims sole credit for the victory before Emperor Reman III, while Vivec and Juilek later meet and negotiate a truce ceding key border fortresses to the Empire in exchange for naval protection and peace.

books.title: 2920, Morning Star
books.summary: Almalexia sends Vivec a prophetic warning that Morrowind will lose the ongoing war unless he retrieves Sotha Sil from Artaeum, while in Black Marsh the exiled Empress Tavia casually discusses assassinating her husband with her loyal Kothringi bodyguard Zuuk. At an Imperial exhibition, Prince Juilek narrowly defeats the Akaviri swordsman Savirien-Chorak in single combat, a match that leaves Emperor Reman III newly suspicious of Potentate Versidue-Shaie's intentions. In Mournhold, the Duke's mistress Turala privately wonders whether he will value her more once he learns she carries his child.

books.title: 2920, Rain's Hand
books.summary: This fourth volume of the 2920 chronicle shows Sotha Sil brokering a pact with eight Daedric Princes to limit their random depredations on mortals, then returning to Artaeum to teach Psijic initiates a fire-resistance restoration charm, during which an overconfident student is badly burned and expelled from training. Elsewhere, Prince Juilek recovers from a long poisoning scare in the Imperial City, and Almalexia arrives at Artaeum to warn Sotha Sil that Morrowind is losing its war and needs him, prompting Master Iachesis to reveal the Psijic Order's coming withdrawal from the world.

books.title: 2920, Second Seed
books.summary: Potentate Versidue-Shaie manipulates Emperor Reman III's fear of court conspiracies while secretly orchestrating events himself, arranging for the poisoner Catchica to be framed and captured along with the Emperor's mistress Rijja. Meanwhile the agent Zuuk hires a boastful mercenary, Miramor, to ambush the Emperor on behalf of the imprisoned Empress Tavia, and Turala, cast out by her family in Mournhold for bearing the Duke of Indoril's child, gives birth alone in the Cyrodiil wilderness with unexpected help from a shapeshifting Ayleid.

books.title: 2920, Sun's Dawn
books.summary: On Artaeum, Sotha Sil teaches Psijic initiates that true Mysticism requires understanding an object's deeper meaning, not just naming it, using a piece of dreugh secretion to illustrate the lesson. Elsewhere, Emperor Reman III grows paranoid about court loyalty while his mistress Rijja calms him, the exiled Turala is branded and cast out of Mournhold's House Redoran, King Dro'Zel of Anequina flies into a violent rage after hearing a tragic bard's tale, and Almalexia senses the Daedra Molag Bal unleashing an attack on the Valenwood town of Gilverdale as she travels toward Artaeum.

books.title: 2920, Sun's Dusk
books.summary: In this eleventh volume of the 2920 chronicle, the Dark Brotherhood's Night Mother accepts a contract from the Argonian agent Zuuk, acting for the late Empress, to have Emperor Reman III assassinated, and lets the overconfident Miramor attempt the killing at the treaty grounds of Bodrum as a test. Miramor is intercepted and killed by an unseen, far more skilled assassin before he can strike the Emperor, confirming the plan's viability. Meanwhile Mehrunes Dagon's forces sack Castle Mournhold, gravely wounding Almalexia in battle before she and Sotha Sil regroup with Vivec, even as the unsuspecting Emperor prepares a treaty-signing ball in the Imperial City.

books.title: 2920, Sun's Height
books.summary: Emperor Reman III and his Potentate discuss the terms of peace with Morrowind while the emperor loses an eye to his imprisoned would-be assassin Rijja after cruelly needling her. In Balmora, Vivec, Sotha Sil, and Almalexia reunite only to learn the Imperial Army has treacherously seized a key fortress despite the truce; when the Duke of Mournhold hires the Morag Tong's Night Mother to have the Emperor killed, Sotha Sil intercepts and sinks the ship carrying the assassins' payment to stop the contract from proceeding.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 1
books.summary: The opening sermon of Vivec's holy autobiography recounts, in dense mystical allegory, the divine origin of Vivec as an androgynous being conceived through Boethiah and a netchiman's wife, gestated among sea creatures under Seht's guidance, and further shaped by seven Daedra and the Demiprince Fa-Nuit-Hen, who teach the unborn Vivec forms of combat. The Daedra prophesy that Vivec is destined to become the Hortator who will lead the Chimer to war against the Indoril within three months. The sermon closes by invoking the triune name ALMSIVI, tying Vivec's mythic birth to the later Tribunal.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 10
books.summary: This cryptic sermon has Vivec instructing the Hortator, Nerevar, to act unseen and effectively unarmed in pursuit of his goals, followed by an invocation attributed to the Daedric Prince Boethiah urging the Chimer, described as devourers of the god Trinimac, to embrace constant change and factional division rather than the stagnation of their enemies. It closes with a fragmented, repetitive litany describing the trickster force Sithis as perpetually in motion, evoking themes of cosmic movement and reflected fate.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 11
books.summary: Framed as counsel Vivec once gave the Hortator during the age of Resdaynia, this sermon delivers cryptic, riddling teachings on the burdens and corrupting temptations of rulership, woven through Tribunal cosmology involving the domains of Ayem and Seht and the shadowy rival figure known as the Sharmat. It closes with paradoxical maxims about weapons, language, and kingship, cast in the deliberately obscure, mystical style typical of Vivec's sermons.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 12
books.summary: In this sermon, the daedra prince Molag Bal ambushes Vivec in the ashlands and severs his feet, but Vivec negotiates a symbolic marriage with Bal, granting him an hour's dominion over his own severed head in exchange for a secret word of royal power. Their union is said to have produced thousands of monstrous offspring, the mightiest of whom is known only by a cryptic name of power too dangerous to speak in full.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 13
books.summary: A cryptic sermon in which Vivec instructs the Hortator, Nerevar, in mystical symbolism -- a 'magical cross' surrounded by a triangle representing the Four Corners (Bal, Dagon, Malacath, Sheogorath) and the ALMSIVI triad -- framing himself as 'the sword' who must eventually be removed from the world for its ending to be fulfilled. He warns that he will repeatedly test and even symbolically kill the ruling king to teach this lesson, and alludes to the Sharmat sleeping at the world's center as the false dreamer who resists this removal.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 14
books.summary: This sermon recounts Vivec's mythic union with the Daedric Prince Molag Bal, whose offspring provoke conflict with a rival Daedra lord, followed by Molag Bal teaching Vivec a forbidden ritual magic that spawns a monstrous, destructive race from the coupling of onlooking Velothi and daedra. Enraged at the devastation this causes, Vivec forges a terrible spear-weapon called Muatra from a secret taken from Molag Bal, uses it to exterminate the monstrous offspring one by one, and vows never again to regard Molag Bal favorably.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 15
books.summary: In this sermon Vivec counsels the Hortator on the perils of rulership, warning that his greatest enemy will be the deceptive Sharmat, who delivers a lengthy, cryptic first-person boast about bringing light, stars, and ruin into the world. Vivec instructs the Hortator that he may one day need to confront this enemy unarmed, gives him words of power to speak in that confrontation, and frames the burden of kingship as an uncertain and perilous path.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 16
books.summary: Nerevar finds Vivec having his hair shorn while practicing the truthful "Water Face," and Vivec urges him toward violent clarity rather than doubt. Nerevar selects an axe and travels to the moon, where the Parliament of Craters denies his authority as Hortator and mocks his claim to greatness; he attacks and largely destroys them, and a surviving voice among the craters rebukes him for leaving behind only graves rather than true legend.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 17
books.summary: This sermon follows Vivec leading a humbled Nerevar (called the Hortator) on a journey across foreign lands to study different fighting traditions, including the blade arts of the serpent-folk Tsaesci of Akavir. Their travels eventually circle back to Red Mountain, where rather than face the Sharmat before the time is right, the two spar with each other, and Nerevar collects mystical "spokes" that Vivec forbids him from assembling into a completed whole.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 18
books.summary: In this sermon, Vivec resolves to begin recording his mystical Book of Hours before the war against the Dwemer, telling Ayem he intends to battle nine escaped monstrous creations, though she cryptically warns he will find only eight since the ninth is already undone by his own decision. The two engage in an abstract dialogue about obsolescence and identity, with Vivec questioning whether an old ideal can be replaced by something merely suited to a changing world, foreshadowing his eventual transformation, and the sermon closes by declaring itself forbidden and untrue.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 19
books.summary: Vivec, donning his armor, enters a vast non-physical realm holding all mortal minds and perceives an ominous 'two-headed king' wearing a crown of shackle-like gems, then builds a symbolic dwelling from which to watch the coming age. He describes its four cornerstones through riddling verse about buried, hidden protective objects, each meant to guard the dwelling, though the sermon closes on an unresolved, repeated doubt about whether that protection truly holds.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 2
books.summary: This sermon recounts the mystical gestation of the egg of Vivec, carried by the netchiman's wife, as a procession of primordial spirits visit and test the unborn god-poet with gifts and riddles. The sixth spirit, Mephala, cuts the egg from the womb to teach it her secret crafts of seduction and killing before returning it blinded, leaving Vivec bound to secret knowledge of the world's creation and its eventual unraveling.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 20
books.summary: In this mystic sermon, the warrior-poet Vivec battles his own monstrous offspring, a shapeshifting being called Moon Axle who is immune to straight weapons like spears due to its ever-changing linear nature, and defeats him only by wielding a curved sword. After binding the wounded creature with captured spirit-souls until it becomes rigid and shatters, Vivec has Velothi philosophers craft its remains into ceremonial wheels, founding what becomes known as the first Whirling School of mystic teaching.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 21
books.summary: A dense scriptural passage called the Scripture of the Wheel describes eight cosmic components of primordial chaos tied to the Aedra, and sixteen intervening spaces associated with Daedric princedoms. It builds toward an esoteric vision of a hidden triangular gate and a tower nested within a tower, said to represent the single true name of God, continuing the layered, riddling symbolism typical of Vivec's sermons.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 22
books.summary: In this sermon, Vivec confronts an undead guardian of House Mora over a relic called the Treasure Wood Sword, said to grant self-knowledge to its wielder, and reclaims it through cryptic ritual speech invoking the goddess Ayem. He then takes the deadliest members of the assassin cult the Morag Tong as consorts, fathering their murderous 'King of Assassins,' who ultimately delivers Vivec the recovered sword after brutally killing the prince of House Mora who had withheld it.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 23
books.summary: Framed as a "Scripture of the Sword," this sermon offers eight cryptic numbered pronouncements attributed to Vivec that use swordsmanship as a metaphor for lawmaking, tireless endurance, trained instinct, and the cutting away of rival creation myths, ending on the image of a road-length blade that only a warrior of true stature can wield.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 24
books.summary: In this sermon, Vivec confronts a monstrous, army-shaped foe called Horde Mountain, which loyal Velothi tribes help ensnare in his honor; he elevates these tribes into a new order, the Buoyant Armigers, then destroys the monster with his weapon Muatra. Its scattered remains become the foundation of the City of Swords — Vivec City itself — which Almalexia and Sotha Sil then bless with protection and a secret word of passage.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 25
books.summary: In this visionary sermon, Vivec describes his own transformation into the living city of Vivec, portraying its streets, temples, and markets as extensions of his own body and the ceaseless trade and worship of its inhabitants as what keeps him 'trans-immortal.' The god-city is depicted simultaneously as ruler, marketplace, and monument to himself.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 26
books.summary: This sermon describes Vivec stalking the fourth of eight mythic monsters, the Pocket Cabal, which lay hidden within forbidden spell-texts studied by eastern Chimer wizards. Moving in disguise, Vivec smuggles a construct into the wizards' libraries to steal the cabal's dangerous knowledge, unleashing chaos among possessed slaves and summoned entities before he slays the wizard who confronts him. He then seals the monster inside a demon-guarded dome and entrusts its safekeeping to his sibling Seht (Sotha Sil).

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 27
books.summary: A cryptic sermon from Vivec's scripture, framed as 'The Scripture of the Word,' offering paradoxical teachings about language, silence, and hidden meaning. It declares that speech is rooted in flesh, that true understanding lies beyond mere articulation, and warns against complacently relying on fixed stories or maps in place of direct, eaten experience.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 28
books.summary: This sermon recounts Vivec's battles against "The Ruddy Man," a monstrous suit of living armor descended from a discarded image of Molag Bal, first destroyed near Gnisis in a clash said to have carved out the West Gash, then re-encountered near Tear after treacherous dreughs corrupt it further and it destroys three villages. Vivec ultimately gifts the creature's carapace to the mystic "Number Room," whose sages ritually transform it into sacred philosopher's armor.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 29
books.summary: This sermon consists of a numbered catalogue titled the Scripture of the Numbers, listing thirty-six mystical concepts within Vivec's cosmology, such as the Dragon Break, the Enantiomorph, the Corners of the House of Troubles, and the Hours, each paired with an obscure numeric value. It closes with a brief gloss dismissing rigid numerology as a prideful, inadequate mortal attempt to pin down divine truths.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 3
books.summary: Vivec's third sermon recounts his mythic origin: his blind mother, the netchiman's wife, is captured by Dwemer who try to cut the divine egg she carries out of her by blade, sound, and fire, all to no avail, until she dies peacefully under a protective incantation. The infant Vivec is then preserved in a magical vessel for study and unsettles his Dwemer captors by expressing the concept of love, something wholly foreign to them, prompting them to relocate his image and speak of coming doom at the hands of the Velothi.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 30
books.summary: Vivec, frustrated at being unable to locate a hidden threat called City-Face, kills a questioning mystic in anger and is rebuked by Nerevar, the Hortator. The sermon explains that City-Face began as a nascent power that grew unnoticed among settled peoples until it was seized by extradimensional beings called the Grabbers, who then confront Vivec intending to replace his city with their own. Vivec corrects their underlying error and kills their leader with a short blade called the Ethos Knife.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 31
books.summary: The Hortator, now married to Ayem, worries that his teacher Vivec has grown distant amid a struggle against Dwemer-stirred monsters; Ayem shows him where Vivec sits, writing privately in his 'Book of Hours' after donning ritual guises tied to memories of his forced marriage to Molag Bal. Vivec first writes a doubting passage admitting the et'Ada are flawed and unreliable, then blots it out and replaces it with a more defiant verse casting himself as a hammer-forged figure who bears a painful truth that others must be broken to hear.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 32
books.summary: Framed as the 'Scripture of the Mace,' this sermon offers eight numbered, riddling aphorisms on themes of self-annihilation, mortal suffering as an imposed condition, the Dunmer's ashen transformation as a mark of their exodus, and the Daedra's role as necessary, radical critics within the cosmic order, delivered in Vivec's characteristically paradoxical and elliptical style.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 33
books.summary: Sermon 33 of Vivec's esoteric scripture recounts the god's hunt for the seventh of his monstrous offspring, a flying creature called Lie Rock, accidentally loosed by a member of a forgotten guild. Vivec pins the monster above the city that bears his name and, with the aid of an ash-king, destroys it — the sermon frames the petrified remainder as a warning suspended over the city (the origin of the Ministry of Truth). Like the rest of the Lessons, it wraps Tribunal theology in riddling, mystical language.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 34
books.summary: Vivec brings the Hortator Nerevar to the Provisional House to witness the defeat of the eighth and final monster standing in the way of founding the city of Narsis. Rather than fighting, Vivec offers the monster gentle consolation so that it willingly accepts death (Muatra) and becomes the city's foundation, prompting Nerevar to question Vivec's methods and ultimately accept his own destined role as the mightiest of Vivec's children.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 35
books.summary: Titled "The Scripture of Love," this cryptic sermon has Vivec meditating in dense, riddling language on love as inseparable from sacrifice, myth, and cosmic ritual, framing his own future reign as an act of transcendent love bound up with coming catastrophe. It closes by attributing the sermon's authority to Mephala as the origin of sex and murder, portraying love as a perilous path that consumes those who pursue it.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 36
books.summary: This final sermon narrates the mythic war between the Chimer and their former Dwemer allies, led respectively by the Hortator Nerevar and King Dumac, ending in Nerevar's killing of Dumac and the Dwemer priest Kagrenac's activation of a great artifact modeled after Vivec's own form. The resulting cataclysm at Red Mountain erases the Dwemer from existence and creates the Inner Sea, after which the united ALMSIVI trio briefly merges and consumes the resulting blight-ash to protect the world from its taint.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 4
books.summary: In this riddling sermon, the unborn Vivec, still carried within the body of the netchiman's wife, is tested by a procession of allegorical spirits on the journey toward Indoril lands. Vivec dismantles a group personifying coincidence by arguing that repeated chance collapses into meaningful pattern, consumes wisdom from an entity called the Old Bone to claim kingship over the world, and outmaneuvers a spirit of rigid certainty by embracing deliberate ambiguity as a source of power.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 5
books.summary: A collapsed Dwemer-built simulacrum of the disguised Vivec, resembling the netchiman's wife, is found by a merchant caravan; a Chimeri warrior urges taking it to Almalexia in the capital, but the merchant captain wants to sell it for profit at Noormoc instead. When the captain refuses Nerevar's offer to simply buy the caravan outright, Vivec speaks cryptically into Nerevar's mind, and Nerevar kills the merchant and seizes the caravan for himself.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 6
books.summary: A dense, riddling sermon in which Vivec, speaking as "Vehk," declares himself the divine "Son" set alongside Boethiah, Azura, and Mephala, weaving sword and word together as parallel routes to enlightenment. He describes guardians and trials meant to test the reader's understanding, presenting the sermon itself as an esoteric puzzle rather than a straightforward lesson.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 7
books.summary: In this sermon, a scamp lord called the Duke of Scamps presents his demonic legions to Mehrunes Dagon's court, seeking permission to destroy Nerevar and the rising Tribunal faith, but Dagon's major domo judges the offered forces insufficient against the Hortator's growing wisdom. A strange vision follows depicting Nerevar's fate entangled with cosmic guardian stars, and the sermon closes with Dagon's servants inscribing a mystic curse-phrase of power onto the Hortator's own hands.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 8
books.summary: This mystic sermon recounts Nerevar and Vivec's ceremonial arrival at the Dunmer capital, where the goddess-figure Ayem receives Nerevar bearing a symbolic relic tied to Vivec's own strange origin. In a riddling exchange, Nerevar declares his intent to adopt Dwemer methods without shame for the coming war, and Seht and Vivec affirm this course through esoteric declarations, framing the moment as fated preparation for the Tribunal's eventual transformation and the war against the Dwemer.

books.title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 9
books.summary: This sermon describes Vivec guiding the Hortator and the Chimer into alliance with the Dwemer against five demon chieftains of the invading northern men. It details Hoaga, who reanimated fallen soldiers with earth; Chemua, who devoured a Chimeri hero; Bhag, who out-debated even Vivec; Barfok, who could sing battles into victory; and Ysmir the Dragon of the North, whom the Hortator wrestled bare-handed before Vivec bound his terrible roar into an ebony frame to drive him away.

books.title: A Dance in Fire, Chapter 1
books.summary: Decumus Scotti, a mediocre clerk dismissed from the Atrius Building Commission, steals blank contracts and joins a caravan to Valenwood to chase a business lead from a disreputable former colleague. Along the way, his camp is raided by acrobatic Cathay-raht -- feline cousins of the Khajiit -- who loot supplies with astonishing leaping agility, terrifying Scotti and his oblivious traveling companion, the poet-scholar Gryf Mallon.

books.title: A Dance in Fire, Chapter 2
books.summary: Imperial clerk Decumus Scotti, traveling as a representative of the Atrius Building Commission, has his caravan looted by Khajiit raiders near the Valenwood border and must pay Bosmer escorts to guide his shrunken group through the jungle. Reaching the mile-tall mobile tree-city of Falinesti, he gets swept into a drunken revel on fermented pig's milk and passes out in a dangerous alley known as the western cross, where giant insects called hoarvors nearly kill him before hunters intervene. Battered but alive, he finally reaches Mother Pascost's Tavern in search of his contact, a man named Jurus.

books.title: A Dance in Fire, Chapter 3
books.summary: Imperial clerk Decumus Scotti follows a barely legible note to the Valenwood river town of Athay, hiring the drunken ex-pirate Captain Balfix, only to arrive as Khajiiti raiders burn the village in a renewed war with Elsweyr. Fleeing burning arrows and a stalking pride of Senche-Tigers, Scotti swims for his life downriver, loses Balfix to drowning, and washes ashore among Bosmer refugees who share roasted Senche-Tiger meat. The chapter ends with Scotti resolving to press on to the town of Vindisi in search of his missing associate Liodes Jurus.

books.title: A Dance in Fire, Chapter 4
books.summary: Fleeing a Khajiit raid alongside Bosmer refugees, clerk Decumus Scotti reaches the sacred village of Vindisi, where the natives enter a living tree-temple to invoke an ancestral guardian force known as the Wild Hunt. When Khajiiti raiders infiltrate the village that night, Scotti and a rival clerk named Reglius hide in a treetop nest; Reglius falls to his death fleeing the attackers, and the unleashed Wild Hunt erupts as a horde of monstrous spirits that devours raiders and refugees alike before the Khajiiti seal the valley shut, trapping the rampage inside as Scotti barely escapes over a cliff.

books.title: A Dance in Fire, Chapter 5
books.summary: Imperial clerk Decumus Scotti, lost and starving in the war-ravaged jungles of Valenwood, is tormented by nonsense-babbling mimic creatures before a mudslide dumps him near a burned-out fishing village destroyed by Khajiiti raiders. There he restrings a bone bow and, after failed attempts, finally kills one of the mimics for food using archery form he half-remembers from watching soldiers in Falinesti. A passing boat carrying the eccentric translator Gryf Mallon rescues him and carries him upriver through a land torn by war on every border, finally reaching the crystalline city of Silvenar, where Scotti is reunited with his fellow clerk Liodes Jurus.

books.title: A Dance in Fire, Chapter 6
books.summary: Imperial clerk Decumus Scotti, having survived disaster in war-torn Valenwood, is coached by fellow building-commission agent Liodes Jurus and the Bosmer merchant Basth into swindling the Silvenar, the mystical ruler whose body and mood mirror the whole Wood Elf people, into signing lucrative reconstruction contracts. Playing a role of studied indifference as instructed, Scotti wins a private audience, secures a sweeping construction deal by deflecting the ruler's anxious question about Imperial intervention, and leaves noting that the diminutive Silvenar seems to have shrunk further under the weight of his people's suffering.

books.title: A Dance in Fire, Chapter 7
books.summary: At a banquet hosted by the Silvenar, Decumus Scotti drunkenly boasts to foreign diplomats about how he secured lucrative rebuilding contracts through simple mercantile instinct rather than skilled diplomacy. Sent home with signed contracts, he becomes the prize in a bidding war between rival patrons Lord Atrius and Lord Vanech, profiting handsomely once Atrius dies in a suspicious accident hinting at the Dark Brotherhood's involvement. The chapter closes on a horrifying note when Scotti realizes a delicacy served at his celebratory feast, supplied by the Silvenar, is made from the remains of his companions Jurus and Basth, left behind in Valenwood.

books.title: A Dark Brotherhood Contract
books.summary: A formal Dark Brotherhood writ, issued under the Night Mother's sanction, authorizing its bearer to have a named target executed on behalf of an anonymous contracting party, invoking the guild's binding traditions and obligations to fulfill the killing by any expedient means.

books.title: A dying man's last words
books.summary: A trapped, dying tomb-robber named Indie reflects on his life of adventure and treasure-hunting, his own father who shared the same calling, and the students he once taught, while resigning himself to death crushed under rubble alongside his gear, including his signature hat. The note plays as a broad comic homage to a famous fictional archaeologist-adventurer rather than a serious in-world account.

books.title: A Fair Warning
books.summary: An adventurer's cautionary account of exploring the flooded Lower Dubdilla caverns, warning would-be treasure hunters about sheer ravines, unstable footing, and vicious winged, fanged creatures lurking in the dark passages. The author credits their own spells, scrolls, and potions with narrowly saving them from disaster and stresses that only well-prepared adventurers carrying emergency remedies should attempt the depths.

books.title: A Game at Dinner
books.summary: A spy embedded among Prince Hlaalu Helseth's court advisors, reporting secretly to House Dres, describes a tense banquet at which Helseth reveals he has laced the table's cutlery (not the food) with poison to smoke out disloyal counselors and rival houses' agents. When the chamberlain Burgess panics and drinks the tureen's antidote, he is exposed as a spy for Queen Elysana of Wayrest and dies in agony, while the letter's author escapes detection and begs to be pulled from the assignment. A publisher's foreword frames the whole letter as an ambiguous work privately circulated by Helseth and his mother Barenziah, which House Dres has publicly disavowed.

books.title: A Hypothetical Treachery
books.summary: Four adventurers -- battlemages Malvasian and Inzoliah, healer Dolcettus, and barbarian Schiavas -- flee the forest of Eldengrove carrying a chest containing the Ebony Mail when a draining ghost kills Dolcettus and Schiavas. As the surviving battlemages trek onward, they trade coy "hypothetical" musings about how one might betray the other for the loot and their single healing potion. Inzoliah secretly casts a slow life-draining curse on Malvasian, and though she later drives off bandits attacking him, he dies from her spell anyway, confirming she out-schemed him from the start.

books.title: A Leaflet
books.summary: A vitriolic flyer warning townsfolk to avoid a merchant named Aurane Frernis, accusing her of selling shoddy and dangerous alchemical goods, and quoting several harsh, mocking customer testimonials meant to ruin her reputation.

books.title: A Less Rude Song
books.summary: A comic, mocking verse arguing that the notorious licentiousness of the Iliac Bay region is tame compared to what can supposedly be found in Morrowind, where Dunmer modesty about nudity is claimed to mask far stranger appetites. Each stanza builds toward a repeated punchline insisting that whatever unusual desire the listener has, Morrowind can satisfy it.

books.title: A scrawled note
books.summary: A tomb raider's final note explaining that his companion Morty died carrying the key needed to enter a sealed tomb, forcing him to attempt to force the door alone despite fearing traps he feels unqualified to disarm. He warns that a valuable prize, called the Staff of Hasedoki, likely lies beyond a dangerous guardian, and bids farewell to a woman named Carmella.

books.title: A scroll written in blood
books.summary: A dying note left by the thief Malaki the Lightfooted, trapped with a broken back in a tomb, reflecting on his lonely life and his one lost love, Mariah of Stros M'kai, while warning other thieves to abandon the profession as he awaits being finished off by approaching undead.

books.title: A Short History of Morrowind
books.summary: This excerpt traces the Dunmer from the prophet Veloth's exodus through the rise of the Great House clans and the Tribunal Temple theocracy, to Morrowind's treaty-based incorporation into Tiber Septim's Empire. It then details the 3E 414 reorganization of Vvardenfell into separate administrative zones for Hlaalu, Redoran, and Telvanni, plus an Imperial zone and a Temple-run zone, contrasting aggressive Hlaalu and Telvanni expansion with conservative Redoran and Temple resistance, and warns that House rivalries, Ashlander raids, and the worsening blight from Red Mountain threaten to force an evacuation of the district.

books.title: A worn and weathered note
books.summary: An anonymous, unnamed narrator delivers a mournful, image-heavy monologue about being torn from a beloved life and pulled into a cold, unfamiliar existence, describing a fall into water as the moment everything changed. The piece dwells on fading memory, numb grief, and the struggle to feel real again, ending on an unanswered plea addressed to an unnamed listener, without identifying any specific person, place, or event.

books.title: Aedra and Daedra
books.summary: This concise essay clarifies that Aedra and Daedra are precise Elvish terms rather than synonyms for gods and demons, with Aedra roughly meaning ancestors and Daedra meaning not our ancestors. It explains the Dunmer cosmological split between the static, creating Aedra, who are bound to the world and can be killed, citing Lorkhan and the creation of the moons as an example, and the changeable, uncreating Daedra, who can only ever be banished, never destroyed.

books.title: Airship Captain's Journal
books.summary: Captain Roberto Jodoin's journal chronicles an expedition aboard an unstable experimental airship, commissioned by the mage Beauchamp to retrieve a magic item from a barrow hidden within the Hrothmund's Bane rock formation on Solstheim. The craft deteriorates in flight, a panicked crewman is killed and lost overboard, and after reaching the formation the expedition is caught in a violent blizzard that crashes the airship and kills the crew. The captain's increasingly incoherent final entries describe him freezing to death alone, hallucinating approaching wolf eyes.

books.title: Ajira's Flower Report
books.summary: Writing in broken Common Tongue, the Mages Guild alchemist Ajira reports on experiments combining several Vvardenfell flowers (among them a spiny yellow bloom, a heavy dark-blue petal, a tall red-flowered plant, and a pink Skyrim-like bloom) with other reagents to brew potions for strength, magicka, disease cure, anti-paralysis, weightlessness, and personality restoration. The report ends with Ajira's irritated complaint that a rival apprentice named Galbedir was assigned less work, paired with confidence that a promotion to Journeyman is imminent.

books.title: Ajira's Mushroom Report
books.summary: A Mages Guild journeyman report in which the alchemist Ajira catalogues four mushrooms found along the Bitter Coast -- Luminous Russula, Violet Coprinus, Bungler's Bane, and Hypha Facia -- noting their appearance, dangerous mixtures, and useful ingredient pairings she discovered through testing, including combinations that grant water breathing and water walking. Ajira closes by arguing she has earned promotion ahead of a rival guildmate named Galbedir.

books.title: Ancestors and the Dunmer
books.summary: This overview explains Dunmer ancestor veneration, describing how households keep shrines where relatives seek counsel and blessing from deceased kin, and how the bones of especially honored dead can be bound into protective ghost fences, the largest example being the Tribunal's Great Ghost Fence around Red Mountain. It also covers spirits forced to linger against their will, who often turn mad or dangerous, and contrasts Dunmer customs with Altmer and Bosmer funerary beliefs and with outsiders' mistaken association of the practice with necromancy, noting that Telvanni sorcerers reserve true necromancy for non-Dunmer remains. A closing publisher's note observes that these traditions have faded since most ancestral remains now go toward maintaining the Ghostfence.

books.title: Antecedants of Dwemer Law
books.summary: A scholarly treatise arguing that Dwemer legal customs descend from Altmeri and Bosmeri traditions of liability and compensation for slaves and animals, citing case law such as Karndar Watch precedents on payment owed when a slave kills a free owner or when a work-site Animunculi kills a laborer. It contrasts these formalized compensations with the harsher, more superstitious blood-revenge customs attributed to Argonians and the Tenmar forest tribes.

books.title: Arcana Restored
books.summary: A mock-archaic instructional pamphlet by the self-important Wapna Neustra on recharging enchanted items at a "Mana Fountain" using pure gold, warning readers of dangerous magical backlash and insisting his method is the only correct one while gleefully disparaging rival authors Kharneson and Rattor as jealous frauds.

books.title: Arkay the Enemy
books.summary: A necromantic lord addresses his followers, naming the god Arkay his eternal rival because Arkay's Law and Blessing protect the dead from being raised or having their souls harvested without consent. He instructs necromancer scholars to undermine Arkay's priests and burial customs, orders priests to keep undead servants hidden while recruiting vampires and liches to their cause, and calls on hidden followers to prepare for a coming campaign to destroy Arkay's temples and erase his worship.

books.title: Ascadian Isles Land Deed
books.summary: A legal deed recording the sale of land south of Arvel Manor and near Pelagiad from Rovone Arvel to Orvas Dren, with Arvel retaining rights to one small farm currently held by the tenant Llovyn Andus.

books.title: Ashland Hymns
books.summary: This small collection of Ashlander folk verse includes 'Wondrous Love,' credited to the Urshilaku tribe, a short devotional lyric celebrating an enduring, faithful romantic bond between two people that lasts from their earliest days together to their final moments.

books.title: Aurane Frernis' Recipies
books.summary: This short alchemical guide lists tested recipes using Vvardenfell ingredients: a restore health potion from marshmerrow, wickwheat, and resin; and a restore fatigue potion from scrib jelly and scuttle, or alternatively stronger but foul-tasting hound meat. It closes by noting that customers generally prefer better-tasting potions over ones that are only marginally more effective.

books.title: Aurane Frernis' Recipies
books.summary: An alchemist's recipe for curing common diseases by heating equal parts gravedust and green lichen until the mixture browns, with a note that daedra skin works as a costlier substitute and chokeweed as an emergency alternative. Separate notes describe ongoing experiments toward a blight-cure using scrib jelly and ash salts, acknowledging the ratio still needs refinement for full effectiveness.

books.title: Aurane Frernis' Recipies
books.summary: An alchemist's recipe for a water-breathing potion made by crushing luminous russula fungus and hackle-lo leaves into a paste, with a note to find an ingredient that improves its flavor. A second recipe for a levitation potion combines coda flowers with either cliff racer plumes or trama root, with a caution never to mix the latter two ingredients together.

books.title: Azura and the Box
books.summary: In this Dwemer folk tale, the elderly scholar Nchylbar seeks final proof of the true limits of divine knowledge, and convinces a reluctant priest friend to help him summon Azura before an audience of his students. Nchylbar presents the goddess with a sealed box and asks her to name its contents; she correctly names an object that is not actually inside, and when he reveals the box is empty, Azura vanishes without acknowledging the trick, leaving Nchylbar content in his skepticism and dead by that same night. A publisher's note compares differing Dunmer and Aldmeris versions of the tale, in which Azura instead recognizes the deception and curses those responsible.

books.title: Beram Journal Entry 1
books.summary: A construction foreman's brief journal entry describing the completion of a dungeon's jail rooms and cells being built for the Telvanni, interrupted when magical roots from a wizard's tower overhead burst through the wall and destroyed two of the cells. He resolves to ask the Telvanni to curb the interference before his crew continues excavating the next section.

books.title: Beram Journal Entry 2
books.summary: A mining foreman's journal entry describes slow progress digging through unusually hard rock possibly near lava flows, prompting the crew to detour through a softer section of cave while awaiting new tools. He dismisses his workers' unease over faint tremors as harmless Telvanni magical activity nearby, and treats rats and insects infesting the dig as a minor annoyance rather than a genuine threat.

books.title: Beram Journal Entry 3
books.summary: A mining foreman named Beram records disaster striking his crew when a collapsing ceiling destroyed their main ramp and killed two workers, leaving the survivors trapped underground with dwindling water. He voices mounting distrust of the wizards who had claimed the excavation site was secure, and describes rising heat and increasingly aggressive vermin as two men are sent further into the caves to search for another way out.

books.title: Beram Journal Entry 4
books.summary: A panicked journal entry from a survivor who discovers the mutilated remains of a companion named Norvus in a chamber being invaded by growing roots and shifting, animate stone. Terrified for both life and sanity as tremors and heat intensify around them, the writer begs for rescue and questions what magical experiment could have caused the disaster.

books.title: Biography of Barenziah v I
books.summary: Recounts Barenziah's early years as the young queen of Mournhold after Tiber Septim's conquest of Morrowind, her placement for safekeeping with retired officer Count Sven Advensen's family in the Skyrim town of Darkmoor, and her contented upbringing there. At sixteen, a manipulative stable boy named Straw convinces her that her guardian intends to sell her into concubinage abroad, prompting the pair to flee in disguise through Whiterun and eventually settle in Rifton.

books.title: Biography of Barenziah v II
books.summary: Continues the young Barenziah's story after her parents fell to Tiber Septim: raised by Count Sven of Darkmoor, she is deceived into fleeing with the stable boy Straw, who falls in with the Khajiit thief Therris to rob the Imperial Commandant's house in Rifton. Barenziah exposes the plot out of loyalty to the Empire, is taken into the care of General Symmachus, and is raised at the Imperial Court alongside Tiber Septim's family until her eighteenth birthday, when she departs to reclaim the throne of Mournhold.

books.title: Biography of Barenziah v III
books.summary: This volume covers Queen Barenziah's marriage to Imperial General Symmachus, the birth of their children Helseth and Morgiah, and the unrest in Mournhold that leads to Symmachus's death fighting rebels. It reveals that the "Emperor" she then sought help from in the Imperial City was actually the impostor Jagar Tharn, who had stolen the Staff of Chaos, and recounts how Barenziah and King Eadwyre of High Rock helped an unnamed Champion recover the Staff's eight scattered fragments to defeat Tharn and free the true Emperor. It closes with Barenziah's remarriage to Eadwyre and her regency over Wayrest while Mournhold awaits her return.

books.title: Biography of the Wolf Queen
books.summary: Chronicles the life of Potema, the Wolf Queen of Solitude, an Imperial princess married young into the Nordic throne of Solitude who used political scheming and a famed speech before the Elder Council to push her son Uriel III's claim, sparking the War of the Red Diamond against Empress Kintyra II. After Uriel III's death, the elderly Potema waged a necromancy-fueled war against her own brothers, Cephorus and Magnus, until she died besieged in her castle in 3E 137.

books.title: Blasphemous Revenants
books.summary: This Dunmer religious tract distinguishes between honorable ancestor spirits, who return unbidden out of love and duty to protect their clan, and the blasphemy of necromancers who forcibly bind the restless dead into servitude, an act treated as an unforgivable sacrilege against the Tribunal and the ancestral Tribes. It closes with a call to violently purge foreign necromancers and vampire lords who hide within Morrowind's shrines to dark spirits, its ancient clan fortresses, and the ruins left by the vanished Dwemer.

books.title: Bloody Note
books.summary: A thief named Jacques writes to an associate, Lucian, reporting the successful haul from a jewelry heist carried out with the help of grahl used to distract or bypass guards, confirming that the crew and their guild have already received their shares. He proposes a follow-up robbery of a lightly-secured museum through a basement window, promising to discuss details in person at an inn in Cyrodiil.

books.title: Bloody Note
books.summary: A brief note from a smuggler named Antoinette to an associate, Borogon, confirms that stolen goods have been hidden in an ice cave and that a contact named Lucian has been informed, while she departs for Summerset Isle with her share of the profits. She also warns him against eating bristleback meat, describing the creatures and their riders as far more dangerous than they appear.

books.title: Boethiah's Glory
books.summary: A short devotional hymn exalts the Daedric Prince Boethiah as a fearsome warrior deity, framing combat and death as sacred and inevitable, and calling on the faithful to accept violence and mortality as expressions of reverence toward her.

books.title: Bone, Part One
books.summary: In a tavern frame story, three drinkers debate the origins of great inventions, prompting Hallgerd to tell the disputed tale of the cruel noble Arslic Oan, whose slave armorer Gorkith is forced to invent bonemold armor under siege by cannibalistic Nords. Successive groups of slaves are sent to fetch water clad first in metal, then leather, then finally bonemold armor, with most devoured along the way before bonemold proves effective enough to let one survivor return.

books.title: Bone, Part Two
books.summary: A grim tale told by the storyteller Hallgerd to companions Xiomara and Garaz, about the besieged lord Arslic Oan, whose armorer Gorkith invents bonemold armor by rendering down the bones of dead slaves so survivors can slip past cannibalistic Nords to fetch water. As more slaves are killed and their bones recycled into armor, the vengeful ghost of a slave named Ponik and others rise from the walls demanding their bones back, killing Gorkith and ultimately reducing Arslic Oan himself to a boneless heap by the time rescuers arrive.

books.title: Book of Life and Service
books.summary: A short liturgical text enumerating a hierarchy of the "Blessed" - Bonemen, Mistmen, Wrathmen, and Masters - each described in a line of scripture praising their form of selfless, eternal service. It closes with a brief call-and-response oath in which servants swear their lives to their Lord, suggesting the devotional structure of a cult hierarchy such as the Sixth House.

books.title: Book of Rest and Endings
books.summary: A cultic ritual text consisting of short, ominous verse invoking the binding and burial of ancient spirits or forebears, calling for their imprisonment deep within the earth and the severing of their power -- read as an obscure rite for laying wrathful ancestral or daedric forces permanently to rest.

books.title: Breathing Water
books.summary: A low-ranking Camonna Tong tax collector known as the Tollman seeks out the sorceress Seryne Relas in Bal Fell to learn a lasting water-breathing spell, intending to dive down to a smuggling ship, the Morodrung, that he had secretly let sink. After weeks of training in the philosophy of Alteration, he descends over several nights and finally reaches the wreck's hold, but becomes so absorbed retrieving a locked box of a drowned sailor's hidden potions that his spell lapses before he can surface, and he drowns within sight of his prize.

books.title: Brief History of the Empire v 1
books.summary: This first volume of an imperial history primer summarizes the Septim dynasty's early rulers, from Tiber Septim's founding of the Third Era through Kintyra II. It covers Pelagius I's assassination by the Dark Brotherhood, the guild-friendly reforms of Uriel I, the corrupt but stabilizing rule of Pelagius II, and the near-loss of Summurset Isle in the War of the Isle under Antiochus. It ends with Kintyra II's capture and death and her cousin's usurpation of the throne as Uriel III, an event that sparked the War of the Red Diamond.

books.title: Brief History of the Empire v 2
books.summary: This chronicle covers the Third Era's War of the Red Diamond, fought between Pelagius II's three children — Potema, Cephorus, and Magnus — which ends with Uriel III's execution and Cephorus I's coronation. It then traces the troubled succession through the elderly Magnus, the erratic Pelagius III (later confined to asylums), the long and celebrated reign of the Dunmer-born Empress Katariah I, the brief rule of Cassynder, and the contested legitimacy of his half-brother Uriel IV.

books.title: Brief History of the Empire v 3
books.summary: This third volume covers the reigns from Uriel IV, whose legitimacy as an adopted, non-blood Septim heir was constantly contested by a powerful Elder Council, through his disinherited son Andorak's revolt and eventual settlement in the kingdom of Shornhelm. It describes Cephorus II's struggle against the Camoran Usurper's undead-and-Daedra army rampaging through Valenwood, and closes with Uriel V's aggressive conquests culminating in his death during a failed invasion of Akavir.

books.title: Brief History of the Empire v 4
books.summary: This installment traces the Septim line from the child-emperor Uriel VI, who eventually broke the Elder Council's grip on power, through his sister Empress Morihatha's successful but measured reconquest of rebellious provinces, cut short by her assassination arranged by a resentful Argonian councilor. It continues through her nephew Pelagius IV's long, stabilizing forty-nine-year reign and into that of the current Emperor, Uriel Septim VII, whose rule was interrupted for a decade when his Battlemage Jagar Tharn imprisoned him and ruled in his place, ending only when an unnamed Champion freed him in 3E 399.

books.title: Brown Book of 3E 426
books.summary: This Telvanni council yearbook for 3E 426 lists the sitting Vvardenfell councilors, Archmagister Gothren and Mage Lords Aryon, Neloth, Dratha, and Therana, along with their towers and appointed mouths in Sadrith Mora. It records the council's formal rebuff of Duke Dren and other Great Houses' complaints about unchecked Telvanni colonization of Vvardenfell's wilderness, and its flat refusal to entertain any restriction on slavery, which it insists is protected under the Treaty of the Armistice.

books.title: Caldera Ledger
books.summary: A mundane ledger recording quantities of ebony mined and shipped from the Caldera mine, with figures that appear unremarkable and show no obvious sign of the illegal shipments rumored elsewhere, possibly evidence that the books have been made to look clean.

books.title: Capn's Guide to the Fishy Stick
books.summary: A joke in-game item framed as the definitive guide to 'fishy sticks' across Tamriel, whose pages are described as too smeared with fishy stick sauce to actually read, making the book's content entirely and comically inaccessible.

books.title: Chance's Folly
books.summary: Balmora's notorious teenage cat-burglar, Minevah 'Chance' Iolos, recruits the seemingly mad Breton warrior Ulstyr Moresby to help her raid the trap-laden Heran Ancestral Tomb, her security expertise disarming locks and traps while his combat skill fells the tomb's guardians. Ulstyr's rambling speech turns out to contain genuine, uncanny foreknowledge of the dungeon, including cryptic warnings about hidden dangers that Chance dismisses as nonsense. She ignores his final warning about a door that becomes an indistinguishable wall, is sealed alone in the treasure vault, and dies there before Ulstyr returns two months later to recover the gold.

books.title: Charwich-Koniinge, Volume 1
books.summary: In a letter to his companion Koniinge, the writer Charwich describes tracking the sorcerer Hadwaf Neithwyr, who once summoned Azura and received her Star on behalf of a shadowy patron named Baliasir. Investigating in a High Rock village, Charwich confronts a cemetery caretaker who transforms into a werewolf, and survives the night by holding the creature at bay unarmed and unarmored until dawn restores the man's humanity and his memories. The caretaker reveals that Baliasir is now courting Queen Elysana in Wayrest, and Charwich sets off to follow the trail toward Azura's Star.

books.title: Charwich-Koniinge, Volume 2
books.summary: Writing to his partner Charwich, the ruthless Koniinge describes his search in Tel Aruhn for the thief Hadwaf Neithwyr, who obtained Azura's Star, aided by a nervous Dissident Priest informant named Minerath. After Charwich's letter brings word of a possible lead involving Neithwyr's sister Peryra, Koniinge tracks Minerath down again, chokes him into submission with bare hands to extract what little he knows, then kills him once the interrogation is finished. He ends unsure of the identity of an associate called Baliasir and plans to follow the trail to High Rock if he hears nothing further.

books.title: Charwich-Koniinge, Volume 3
books.summary: A dying letter from the adventurer Charwich to his companion Koniinge, written as he bleeds out in Wayrest, recounting how he befriended the daedra lord Baliasir, disguised as a courtier, in order to steal Azura's Star, using his knowledge of Mysticism spells like telekinesis and spell reflection to earn Baliasir's trust. When Charwich grabbed the Star and attacked, Baliasir revealed his true daedric form and struck him with a lethal spell; Charwich barely escaped by casting a Mysticism Recall spell back to his last anchor point, but died of the wound before healers could reach him.

books.title: Charwich-Koniinge, Volume 4
books.summary: In a letter left for Lord Gemyn by the estate banker Syrix Goinithi just before his murder, we learn how the treasure hunter Koniinge was tricked by a faked death from his partner Charwich, who together with his new lover Lady Moorling used the recovered Daedric artifact Azura's Star (taken from the slain siblings Hadwaf and Peryra Neithwyr) to build new wealthy identities across Tamriel. After strangling his way through a trail of witnesses to learn the truth, Koniinge tracks Charwich to Syrix's villa, kills Syrix, and lies in wait to ambush his former partner.

books.title: Cherim's Heart of Anequina
books.summary: Imperial University professor Livillus Perus interviews the acclaimed Khajiit tapestry artist Cherim about an early masterwork depicting a decisive battle of the Five Year War between Elsweyr and Valenwood, in which Cherim himself fought as a foot soldier. Cherim explains that after a costly defeat while wearing heavy Nord-style plate at the Battle of Zelinin, Khajiiti forces switched back to traditional medium armor for the war's turning-point battle, valuing its mobility and the way it lets arrows pass cleanly through rather than lodge and reopen wounds. He also points out a self-deprecating self-portrait hidden within the crowded battle scene.

books.title: Children of the Sky
books.summary: An ethnographic account of the Nords describes their self-identity as 'children of the sky' bound to breath and voice, including the practice of weaving defeated enemies' tongues into speech-holding ropes and the use of shout-based powers by elite warriors called Tongues to breach gates, rally troops, or travel instantly. It notes that the most powerful Nords become so destructive in speech that they must be gagged and communicate only through sign language and runes.

books.title: Chimarvamidium
books.summary: As part of a truce ending a Chimer-Dwemer war, the Chimer warlord Sthovin gifts his rival Karenithil Barif a golden armored golem meant to defend against Nord raiders, and Barif's advisors urge him to use it to launch a surprise attack on the newly-armored Dwemer camp instead. The golem malfunctions and turns on the Chimer during the assault, revealing it was secretly operated from within by the Dwemer armorer Jnaggo, allowing Sthovin to foresee and defeat the betrayal. A publisher's note argues the tale is genuinely of Dwemer origin, highlights early Chimer unfamiliarity with full-body armor, and connects the legend's mention of a mysterious 'Calling' to theories about the Dwemer's later disappearance.

books.title: Chronicles of Nchuleft
books.summary: This Dwemer chronicle entry, apparently recorded by an Aldmeri scribe, describes a secretive meeting between Lord Ihlendam and rival dwarven leaders that fueled suspicion of treason from Councilor Bluthanch and her sons, followed by a drunken quarrel at a Council gathering that nearly erupted into open combat between Bluthanch and Ihlendam. When Bluthanch later invites Ihlendam to a parley despite his kin's warnings, he is killed by monsters while traveling through Chinzinch Pass, a death many citizens quietly, though never provably, blamed on Bluthanch's family.

books.title: Client List
books.summary: A merchant or enchanter's order ledger lists pending customer requests for magical goods and materials, including a soul gem filled with a daedra's soul, an enchanted mysticism ring, a steel sparksword, spark-enchanted arrows, an exquisite ring of wildfire, and a set of empty greater soul gems.

books.title: Colony Status Report
books.summary: A brief progress report addressed to a Factor overseeing the Raven Rock colony, noting that mine expansion has raised ore yield by roughly 18 percent and that weekly quotas continue to be met. It also flags two crates of spoiled wickwheat from a recent supply delivery, with a refund from the supplier already arranged.

books.title: Confessions of a Skooma-Eater
books.summary: An anonymous Dunmer preface argues, against common Dunmer belief, that skooma addiction can be overcome not through shame or willpower alone but through honest self-understanding and acceptance of one's own cravings. It introduces the companion narrative by Tilse Sendas, which follows one addict's descent into dependency and eventual path toward recovery, and controversially suggests that giving up skooma entirely is only one legitimate choice an addict might make, a stance that has drawn criticism from conservative segments of Dunmer society.

books.title: Construction Contract
books.summary: A formal grant by which the Duke of Vvardenfell authorizes its bearer to build a stronghold and village of limited size and garrison strength, obligating the recipient to protect the settlers within its bounds and to swear loyalty to both the crown and the Tribunal, on pain of the grant's revocation for any breach of terms.

books.title: Corpse Preparation v I
books.summary: A necromancer's practical, region-by-region guide to acquiring corpses across Tamriel: legal criminal corpses in Cyrodiil, reliance on slaves in Temple-suppressed Morrowind, difficulties in Black Marsh and Valenwood, unusually open study of the dead among Summerset Isle nobility, and the prized durability of Orc remains from newly founded Orsinium. It closes with notes on animating men versus animals, warning that raised animals often fail to distinguish master from prey.

books.title: Corpse Preparation v II
books.summary: This necromancer's instructional volume explains that a raised skeleton servant requires a nearly complete skeleton to function reliably, and recommends reinforcing its joints with leather straps or, more expensively, metal spikes to make it sturdier in combat. It warns novice necromancers against carelessly reanimating skeletons without preparation, since a poorly bound or already-damaged skeleton often cannot be successfully raised a second time.

books.title: Corpse Preparation v III
books.summary: The third volume of a necromancer's practical manual on corpse preparation, covering fresh and lightly decayed corpses. It explains how scavenging animals can strip flesh for skeletal servants, how a destroyed zombie can be repeatedly reanimated by recovering and rebinding its remains, and describes the superior mummification process of salt or natron curing followed by cloth wrapping to produce a stronger, more independent undead servant.

books.title: Cure Blight Potion Notice
books.summary: A shopkeeper named Jolda posts a notice apologizing for irregular restocking of Blight-treatment potions shipped in from Sadrith Mora, urging customers to limit outdoor exposure and recommending resistance potions as prevention alongside a curative remedy once symptoms appear.

books.title: Custom Armor Price List
books.summary: An advertisement for the Indalen family's Mournhold workshop, which offers custom-fitted ebony, glass, and adamantium armor crafted from materials the customer supplies, completed within 24 hours. It lists detailed prices for each armor type's cuirass, pauldrons, bracers, greaves, boots, and helm.

books.title: Custom Fur Armor Price List
books.summary: An advertisement and price list from the Solstheim armorer Brynjolfr, challenging hunters to bring down the island's elusive snow bears and snow wolves for their pelts, which he will craft into custom light fur armor. It itemizes the pelt count and gold cost required for each individual armor piece, from cuirass and pauldrons to gauntlets, greaves, boots, and helm, in both bear and wolf styles.

books.title: Custom Fur Armor Price List
books.summary: A merchant's price list in which the armorer Brynjolfr of Solstheim advertises custom light fur armor crafted from snow bear and snow wolf pelts, challenging hunters to bring him enough pelts and gold for cuirasses, pauldrons, gauntlets, greaves, boots, and helms, since no one has yet managed to hunt enough of the elusive beasts.

books.title: Dagoth Ur's Plans
books.summary: Assembled by Temple scholars and Inquisition agents for Vivec, this intelligence assessment reconstructs Dagoth Ur's goals: raise a new god, Akulakhan, from the Heart of Lorkhan and a Dwemer-built body, install House Dagoth as its priesthood, break the Temple's authority, purge outsiders, and drive out the Empire. It outlines his phased approach of fortifying Red Mountain, recruiting Sleepers and Dreamers through sent dreams, expanding bases such as Kogoruhn and coastal smuggling cells, and escalating to assassination campaigns against Imperial sympathizers. A closing timeline traces events from Dagoth Ur's reawakening through the 3E 417 loss of Sunder and Keening and into the intensifying violence of 3E 426-427.

books.title: Darkest Darkness
books.summary: Explains the distinction between Daedra briefly conjured by sorcerers and those bound to Nirn indefinitely through worship or artifact enchantment, illustrated by long-term examples like Mehrunes' Razor and the Masque of Clavicus Vile. It then lays out the Tribunal Temple's division of lesser Daedra into the loyal "Good Daedra" serving Boethiah, Azura, and Mephala, and the rebellious "Bad Daedra" serving Mehrunes Dagon, Malacath, Sheogorath, and Molag Bal, naming each one's signature servant creature.

books.title: Death Blow of Abernanit
books.summary: This epic poem, annotated with historical footnotes by the sage Geocrates Varnus, recounts Temple commander Rangidil Ketil's 3E 150 siege of Abernanit, a Sixth House stronghold held by the Mehrunes Dagon-worshipping tyrant Dagoth Thras. After Rangidil's finest warriors are cut down one by one trying to reach the tower, he personally duels Dagoth Thras, whose blessed shield deflects every blow for hours, until Rangidil wears him down and finally lands the killing strike once his foe's guard falters.

books.title: decoded package
books.summary: A confidential dispatch from Imperial secretary Glabrio Bellienus to Spymaster Caius Cosades, informing him that the newly-freed prisoner %PCName has been enrolled as a Novice of the Blades under his command. It reveals that the Emperor takes seriously a local legend of an outcast destined to unite the Dunmer tribes as the reincarnated hero Nerevar, and orders Cosades to have %PCName investigate the prophecy and, where possible, fulfill it.

books.title: Deed to Indrele's House
books.summary: A legal deed recording the sale of a house and land in Seyda Neen from Dunmer Indrele Rathryon to buyer Velanda Omani of House Hlaalu, for a price of 3000 Imperial Drakes, formally sealed and dated to the year 3E 426.

books.title: Diary of a Lost Sailor
books.summary: A diary chronicles a shipwrecked sailor's increasingly desperate attempt to lead his stranded crew home after a storm near Ebonheart, as he is repeatedly misdirected by locals and reduced to eating rats and boiling his own shoes for broth. After finally reaching an inland town, he is lured underground by a seemingly helpful stranger, beaten for an offhand remark, and imprisoned in a pit beneath the streets. The final entries describe him trapped and starving as his captors lower a monstrous creature down to him, ending with his resignation to death.

books.title: Directions to Caius Cosades
books.summary: Formal orders instructing a newly released prisoner to travel to Balmora, locate the agent Caius Cosades by asking after him at the South Wall cornerclub, and deliver a sealed package of documents without inspecting its contents. Signed by the Emperor's personal secretary, it frames the mission as repayment of a life-debt to Uriel Septim, with obedience promised reward and betrayal promised a traitor's fate.

books.title: Dispel Potion Formula
books.summary: A concise alchemical formula for a dispel potion, instructing the reader to crush pearl into powder, melt and brown moon sugar, combine the two with water, and then boil and distill the mixture in an alembic to collect the finished potion.

books.title: Dren's Note
books.summary: In this incriminating note signed D, a Hlaalu figure evidently Duke Dren instructs his agents Ranes and Navil that his brother the Duke has been disrupting their smuggling operation and may need to be killed so he can seize the dukedom before House Redoran can name a rival successor. He offers to reward the agents for continued cooperation, or accept their silence if they refuse to take part in the plot.

books.title: Dren's shipping log
books.summary: This ledger records the incoming and outgoing shipments of the Hlaalu magnate Orvas Dren, complete with dates and the names of his business partners, offering a glimpse into the trade dealings of one of Vvardenfell's most influential merchants.

books.title: Dwemer Museum Welcome
books.summary: A brief welcome note from the Telvanni wizard Aryon introduces visitors to his private museum of Dwemer artifacts, describing it as an ongoing collection gathered from ruins throughout Morrowind, and warns guests to be cautious around a malfunctioning centurion on display at the end of the hall.

books.title: East Empire Company Ledger
books.summary: An in-universe merchant ledger format used to track goods the East Empire Company trades in on Vvardenfell, functioning as a bookkeeping record rather than a narrative text.

books.title: EEC Stock Certificate
books.summary: A formal certificate attesting ownership of one hundred shares in the Raven Rock division of the East Empire Company, laying out standard provisions for share transfer under the company's articles of incorporation and signed by a company officer.

books.title: Elante's Notes
books.summary: The excavation journal of a treasure hunter named Elante who, with an assistant Badama, locates and breaks into the sealed tomb of a figure called Mordrin Hanin, using conjured Scamps to dig through Daedric-worked stone blocking the entrance. As they near the buried chambers, Elante grows increasingly paranoid and cruel toward the summoned creatures, killing a fleeing Scamp and hearing voices calling Mordrin's name, all while still searching for the tomb's 'Key Guardian' needed to proceed further.

books.title: Elone's Directions to Balmora
books.summary: A short travel guide gives step-by-step road directions from Seyda Neen to Balmora, citing landmarks such as Pelagiad, the volcanic ravine of Foyada Mamaea, Fort Moonmoth, and crossings of the Odai River, and cautions travelers to watch for signposts and stay on the road in poor weather or darkness.

books.title: Erna's Note to Brandr
books.summary: A short, affectionate note from Erna inviting Brandr to meet her by the banks of the river Isild to discuss their future together and his escape from an unhappy marriage.

books.title: Fall of the Snow Prince
books.summary: A Nord chronicler recounts the climactic Battle of the Moesring on Solstheim, where Nord warriors in the tradition of Ysgramor nearly annihilate the last Elven forces on the island until a mysterious, magically radiant warrior called the Snow Prince rides out and single-handedly slaughters many of the Nords' finest fighters. The battle turns when a grieving twelve-year-old girl, Finna, kills the Snow Prince with her dead mother's sword after watching him strike her mother down. The victorious Nords, awed by his valor, honor their fallen enemy with a lavish barrow burial rather than the customary burning of foes.

books.title: Famed Artifacts of Tamriel
books.summary: A catalog of Tamriel's most storied magical relics, describing the origin legend and special powers of each — armors like the Lord's Mail, Ebony Mail, and Dragonbone Mail, weapons like Chrysamere, Goldbrand, and Mehrunes' Razor, and rings tied to figures such as Syrabane and Phynaster. A recurring theme is that most of these items refuse to stay with one owner for long, vanishing or moving on once their bearer is judged unworthy or the item's patron deity wills it.

books.title: Fellowship of the Temple
books.summary: Archcanon Tholer Saryoni's introductory guide for outsiders considering joining the Tribunal Temple, describing worship of Almalexia, Vivec, and Sotha Sil as mortals who achieved divinity through discipline and virtue, and outlining the traits and skills the faithful are expected to cultivate, including Restoration, Alchemy, Mysticism, and Conjuration. It sets out duties owed to faith, kin, superiors, and the common good, and points readers toward further Temple texts on sermons, saints, and pilgrimage.

books.title: Feyfolken I
books.summary: A frame story in which the Great Sage tells his students about Vanus Galerion's founding of the Mages Guild and its more accessible, mechanized enchanting and alchemy tools, contrasted with the elitist training methods of the Psijic Order. Within that frame, he recounts how a lonely, disease-silenced scribe named Thaurbad, working for a temple of Auri-El in Alinor, sent his servant boy Gorgos to have a quill enchanted at the newly arrived Mages Guild; lacking proper guidance, the initiate there bound the quill with an unusually powerful and little-understood daedric soul called Feyfolken, leaving the quill's actual effects on Thaurbad as a cliffhanger.

books.title: Feyfolken II
books.summary: The Great Sage continues a tale for two young students about Thaurbad, a mute Temple scribe whose enchanted quill, infused with a daedric spirit, transforms his mundane bulletin layouts into dazzling works of art that win him sudden fame and fortune. As the story pauses, the students correctly reason from clues in its style that the spirit possessing the quill, Feyfolken, serves the daedric prince Clavicus Vile and is steadily taking over as the true author of Thaurbad's work.

books.title: Feyfolken III
books.summary: A frame-narrator's Great Sage tells of Thaurbad, a mute Temple scribe whose enchanted quill was bound to the Daedra Feyfolken, servant of Clavicus Vile. After Thaurbad angrily rejects the quill's magic and tries writing plainly, the entity begins twisting his outgoing notes and his own perception of them, driving him step by step toward suicide even as his unwitting assistant delivers his deranged final drafts and death threats to an admiring Temple readership as intentional art. The listeners debate afterward whether Feyfolken serves the mischief of Clavicus Vile or the madness of Sheogorath.

books.title: Fighters Guild Charter
books.summary: The official Imperial charter of the Fighters Guild, establishing its purpose of supplying mercenaries and fulfilling citizen contracts, its legal authority under the Guilds Act as confirmed under Potentate Versidue-Shaie, membership requirements around weapon proficiency and heavy armor use, and a list of its Vvardenfell chapters located in Ald'ruhn, Balmora, Sadrith Mora, and Vivec.

books.title: Five Songs of King Wulfharth
books.summary: Five linked Nordic legends trace the life, death, and rebirth of King Wulfharth of Skyrim: his ascension after defeating the Alessians and his violent restoration of Nordic worship, heroic deeds such as battling Orcs and swallowing a storm cloud, his death after using a newly learned Thu'um to reverse an attack by the god Orkey that had aged the Nords back into children, and his resurrection by the god Shor as the 'Ash King' to fight beside Dagoth Ur's forces against the Dwemer at Red Mountain -- where Dagoth Ur's promise of recovering Shor's Heart proves a trap that dooms Shor's army. A secret final song retells the same battle from a Dunmer perspective, describing Nerevar, Dumac, and Alandro Sul clashing with Lorkhan and Dagoth-Ur, ending with Nerevar cutting Lorkhan's Heart free using Sunder and Keening.

books.title: For my Gods and Emperor
books.summary: A recruitment handbook for the Imperial Cult in Vvardenfell, describing its worship of the Nine Divines and the god-hero Tiber Septim, its core virtues, membership fees and doctrine, and the various ranks of service such as lay healers, almoners, and shrine sergeants. It also lays out the cult's stated relationships with other factions -- friendly toward the Legion, Guilds, and House Hlaalu, disapproving of slavery and the Camonna Tong, and openly antagonistic toward the rival Tribunal Temple.

books.title: For Shara, on my death
books.summary: A grieving suitor's farewell letter to a woman named Shara describes his failed attempts to win her affection through gifts and acts of devotion, including killing a trader who had wronged her, and announces his intention to end his life since she never returned his feelings.

books.title: Fort Pelagiad Prisoner Log
