books.summary: A short administrative record listing two prisoners held at Fort Pelagiad: an Orc jailed after a tavern brawl that damaged furniture and windows at the Halfway Inn, sentenced to work off the cost, and a Bosmer held on charges spanning stealing, robbery, plotting with other criminals, and defying the guards who arrested him.

books.title: Fragment: On Artaeum
books.summary: This fragment describes the Isle of Artaeum, home of the ancient Psijic Order and its philosophy called the Elder Way, noting the island's mysterious five-century disappearance beginning around the founding of the Mages Guild and its equally mysterious reappearance. It outlines the Order's historical influence on emperors and Summurset kings, including a claimed role in destroying an invading fleet, and the more recent estrangement between the Psijics and the last four emperors. The author, writing while a guest on Artaeum, praises the island's beauty and the ancient Ceporah Tower.

books.title: Frontier, Conquest...
books.summary: This university history essay argues that human ('Nedic') settlement of Tamriel long predates Ysgramor, with the ancestors of the Bretons, Cyrodilians, and Redguards already living peacefully alongside Elves in High Rock, Hammerfell, and Cyrodiil generations before his Atmoran migration. It contends the Nords were the only Nedic people to fail at accommodation with their Elven neighbors, instead conquering Skyrim by force under King Harald, while elsewhere intermarriage and coexistence defined early human-Elven relations.

books.title: Galerion The Mystic
books.summary: A biography of Vanus Galerion, born a serf named Trechtus under a nobleman who banned literacy among his subjects; after his father is executed for smuggling books, the boy flees to Summerset Isle, where traveling troubadours discover his sharp mind and a mystic among them, Heliand, brings him to the Isle of Artaeum. There the Psijic magister Iachesis renames him Vanus Galerion and trains him, giving him both the arcane education and the personal conviction about open knowledge-sharing that later leads him to found the Mages Guild.

books.title: Galur Rithari's Papers
books.summary: These private papers of a Buoyant Armiger named Galur Rithari describe his shame after being turned into a vampire of Clan Aundae and his years living apart from society, preying only on beasts. Desperate for a cure, he prays to Molag Bal at a hidden shrine and is offered a bargain: retrieve a cursed soul gem from caverns near Dagoth Ur in exchange for being freed of vampirism. After delivering the gem to the Daedra Prince's altar, Rithari undergoes an agonizing ritual and wakes to find himself human again.

books.title: Ghost-Free Papers
books.summary: This mock inspection certificate humorously declares the Gateway Inn in Sadrith Mora officially free of ghosts and other supernatural nuisances, issued by an absurdly named inspector representing a parody organization with a deliberately ridiculous title. Its closing joke attributes the inn's only remaining bad odor to its own hospitality staff rather than anything otherworldly, poking fun at pompous bureaucratic certificates and magical titles.

books.title: Gnisis Eggmine Pass
books.summary: An official pass authorizes its bearer to enter the Gnisis Eggmine for a regular work shift upon presenting it to the guard, while explicitly forbidding entry to the lower mine because of the risk of spreading blight disease, signed by local officials.

books.title: Grasping Fortune
books.summary: A House Hlaalu councilor's recruitment pamphlet contrasts Hlaalu's embrace of Imperial law and commerce with the shortcomings of the other Great Houses, arguing that Redoran's martial pride, Telvanni infighting, Indoril's dependence on charity, and Dres's poor relations will all eventually lose out to Hlaalu's adaptability. It advises prospective members to balance profit-seeking with reputation, avoid theft and murder as bad for business, and favor light armor, short blades, and ranged weapons in the House's fast, pragmatic style, directing applicants to the Balmora Council Manor.

books.title: Great Houses of Morrowind
books.summary: An overview of Morrowind's five Great Houses -- Hlaalu, Redoran, Telvanni, Indoril, and Dres -- describing their heraldic colors, core values, and architectural styles. It contrasts House Redoran's duty and piety, House Hlaalu's pro-Imperial pragmatism and openness to other races, House Telvanni's isolationist wizard-lords, and the staunchly traditionalist, Imperial-hostile, slavery-dependent House Indoril and House Dres, neither of which holds land on Vvardenfell.

books.title: Guide to Ald'ruhn
books.summary: This traveler's guide surveys Ald'ruhn, seat of House Redoran, breaking it into the main town, the councilor district sheltered under a colossal fossilized crab shell, and the Imperial garrison at Buckmoth Fort. It lists where to find guild, temple, and merchant services, names the sitting councilors and other prominent local figures, and gives directions and silt strider connections to nearby settlements.

books.title: Guide to Balmora
books.summary: A travel guide to Balmora, seat of House Hlaalu, detailing its four districts -- its districts (upper-class, commercial, and working quarters) plus Fort Moonmoth -- and where to find guild, Temple, and Legion services. It names notable local figures including the Hlaalu steward Nileno Dorvayn, guild stewards Eydis Fire-Eye, Ranis Athrys, and Ethasi Rilvayn, and the rumored Thieves Guild contact 'Sugar Lips' Habasi, plus transportation routes to other Vvardenfell settlements.

books.title: Guide to Sadrith Mora
books.summary: Describes Sadrith Mora, the island seat of the Telvanni Council, covering its Gateway Inn, Great Market, Council Hall, and Councilor Neloth's tower Tel Naga, alongside the outlander-facing guild services housed at Wolverine Hall. It also lists notable local figures and explains that, having no mainland road, the settlement is reached only by ship or Mages Guild teleportation.

books.title: Guide to Vivec
books.summary: A travel guide surveying Vivec City's eight cross-shaped cantons, from the tourist-oriented Foreign Quarter and the Temple Compound housing the High Fane, Ministry of Truth, and Palace of Vivec, to the Great House compounds of Hlaalu, Telvanni, and Redoran and the commoner districts of St. Delyn and St. Olms. It also notes prominent local figures and details transport links by bridge, silt strider, ship, and canal gondola.

books.title: Guide to Vvardenfell
books.summary: A geographic and administrative overview of Vvardenfell Island, describing its nine distinct regions -- the Ascadian Isles, Ashlands, Azura's Coast, Bitter Coast, Grazelands, Molag Amur, Red Mountain, West Gash, and Sheogorad -- and cataloging the major settlements, Great House seats, Ashlander camps, and Imperial outposts found within each. It notes the island's isolation behind the Inner Sea, its recent opening to settlement, and the volcanic Red Mountain that dominates its interior.

books.title: Guylaine's Architecture
books.summary: This excerpt from Guylaine Marilie's architectural reference explains a Second Empire Dwemer design convention called the Four Tests, a formal philosophy for structural approaches and defenses: recognizing hidden patterns, methodically working through unordered tasks, seeking a path around obstacles, and, failing that, confronting them directly. The text notes that House Telvanni later adopted the Four Tests as a decorative and functional element in the approaches to their wizard towers.

books.title: Hallgerd's Tale
books.summary: Three friends debate who deserves the title of greatest warrior, and Hallgerd settles it with the story of Hlaalu Pasoroth, a champion famed for moving with unusual speed and grace despite wearing full heavy mail. When Pasoroth's armorer sabotages his armor's joints so he can seduce Pasoroth's wife during a tournament, the scheme backfires bloodily, and the bawdy tale ends proving Pasoroth's mastery extends to satisfying his wife without ever managing to remove the gummed-up suit.

books.title: handwritten letter
books.summary: In this letter, Bedal Alen writes to his cousin Forven Berano debating who should carry out an assassination against King Helseth, ruling out himself as an unskilled merchant, Forven as an inexperienced fighter, and a crude mercenary named Hloggar the Bloody, while distrusting the Dark Brotherhood as being controlled by Helseth himself. He proposes approaching the more principled Morag Tong instead, laments the public's passive acceptance of Helseth's rule following a recent murder, and suggests recruiting a sympathetic pamphleteer to sway public opinion toward their cause.

books.title: handwritten note
books.summary: A barely legible, heavily misspelled copy of palace guard duty rosters in which three names are consistently spelled correctly -- Milvela Dralen, Ivulen Irano, and Aleri Aren -- and shifts where all three alone guard the Throne Room are conspicuously double-underlined, suggesting a planned conspiracy or crime among them.

books.title: Hanging Gardens...
books.summary: A fragmentary Dwemer text, only partially translatable into Aldmeris, describing a guide leading someone through a ruined town center's gardens and questioning ancient methods of animating constructs and defying ancestral tradition. A later scribal note chastises the original translator, identified only as Nbthld, for producing technically accurate but garbled Aldmeris.

books.title: Hanin's Wake
books.summary: An account of the funeral rites held for the deceased figure Mordrin Hanin, drawing representatives from several ancient settlements including Ald Sotha to the site of Assurnabitashpi for a mass sacrifice. It records the grim ceremonial recipe for a ritual drink made from sacrificial blood, a daedra heart, and other unsettling ingredients, a mixture so lethal that many mourners died from drinking it and were said to join Hanin in death.

books.title: Hasphat's notes for Cosades
books.summary: Scholar Hasphat Antabolis's briefing notes for the Blades agent Caius Cosades summarize House Dagoth as an extinct Great House whose leaders were exposed as traitors after the Battle of Red Mountain, with the surviving loyal membership redistributed among the other Houses, while the Temple claims the legendary evil beings beneath Red Mountain are that House's original leadership sustained by dark sorcery. The notes also point to several books on the Sixth House and Nerevar obtainable from a bookseller in Vivec's Commercial District.

books.title: Hlaalu Vaults Ledger
books.summary: A dry financial ledger recording commercial transactions conducted through the Hlaalu Vaults, along with a current accounting of the vaults' held inventory.

books.title: Homilies of Blessed Almalexia
books.summary: A collection of short Tribunal Temple parables includes a young Sotha Sil learning that cruelty to lesser creatures causes real suffering, Vivec settling a vanity dispute between two arguing beasts by killing them both, a cautionary tale about a creature that fails to notice gradually rising danger, and Vivec exposing a boastful Telvanni healer's hypocrisy. Further fables describe frightened guar and mudcrabs each fleeing the other in a lesson about perspective, and a wounded netch that dies not from its injury but from companions who take its food instead of helping it.

books.title: Honor Among Thieves
books.summary: A boastful recruiter named Arnie pitches membership in the Thieves Guild, listing the skills it prizes -- stealth, lockpicking, light weapons, and light armor -- alongside practical perks like shared information, safe lodging, and bribed guards. He contrasts the Guild's rule against killing with the murderous, xenophobic Camonna Tong, and directs would-be recruits to seek contacts at cornerclubs in Vvardenfell's major settlements rather than any formal guildhall.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A formal Morag Tong writ naming the wizard Baladas Demnevanni as a lawfully sanctioned target, granting its bearer official license to kill him under the Tong's ancient code.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A brief Morag Tong writ formally sanctioning the killing of one Tirer Belvayn, granting its bearer official license to carry out the execution under the Guild's lawful tradition.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: An official Morag Tong writ formally authorizing its bearer to legally kill a single named target, Mathyn Bemis, under the guild's sanctioned execution tradition.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: This formal Morag Tong writ authorizes its bearer to lawfully execute a named target, Dram Bero, invoking the guild's ancient sanctioned right to kill, and offers no further explanation of the reason for the sentence.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: This formal Morag Tong writ authorizes its bearer to lawfully execute a named target, Brilnosu Llarys, invoking the guild's ancient sanctioned right to kill. As a legal instrument rather than a narrative, it offers no context for the target's offense, only the guild's official license.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A formal Morag Tong writ naming Galasa Uvayn as a lawfully sanctioned target, granting its bearer official license to kill her under the Tong's ancient code.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A formal Morag Tong writ naming Guril Retheran as a sanctioned assassination target, authorizing its bearer to carry out his killing under the guild's traditional, legally recognized code of honor-bound execution.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A formal Morag Tong writ sanctioning the honorable execution of Mavon Drenim, granting the bearer official legal license under Morag Tong tradition to kill the named target.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A Morag Tong writ formally sanctions the killing of two named targets, Navil and Ranis Ienith, certifying under the guild's traditions that the execution is lawfully authorized and granting the document's bearer official license to carry it out.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A formal Morag Tong writ sanctioning the honorable execution of a named target, Feruren Oran, granting its bearer official license to kill in accordance with the guild's lawful traditions and practices.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A Morag Tong writ formally condemning Sarayn Sadus to "honorable execution," certifying its bearer as officially sanctioned to carry out the killing under Morag Tong law.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: An official Morag Tong writ formally sanctioning the honorable execution of a man named Toris Saren, granting its bearer legal license under Morag Tong tradition to carry out the killing.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: This formal Morag Tong writ names Mistress Therana as a sanctioned target, granting whoever carries it legal cover under Guild tradition to carry out her killing as an honorable act rather than common murder.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: This formal Morag Tong writ names Larrius Varro as a sanctioned target, granting whoever carries it legal cover under Guild tradition to carry out his killing as an honorable act rather than common murder.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: An official Morag Tong writ formally authorizing its bearer to legally kill two named targets, Idroso Vendu and Ethal Seloth, under the guild's sanctioned execution tradition.

books.title: Honorable Writ of Execution
books.summary: A formal Morag Tong writ sanctioning the honorable execution of Odaishah Yasalmibaal, granting the bearer official legal license under Morag Tong tradition to kill the named target.

books.title: Hospitality Papers
books.summary: A House Telvanni-issued travel and lodging permit authorizing its bearer to move about Sadrith Mora, meet with residents, and seek lodging in accordance with the Great House Telvanni's Collective Articles, signed by the Prefect of Hospitality, Master Angaredhel.

books.title: How Orsinium Passed to the Orcs
books.summary: When Breton lord Bowyn and the Orc chieftain Gortwog gro-Nagorm both stake equally valid legal claims to the same tract of land near Wayrest, an ancient law forces them to settle it by single combat in Orcish armor. Bowyn trains under Tunner, his cousin's elderly servant and a former Cursed Legion soldier who once trained Orcs himself, and despite the duel being moved up early and Bowyn overindulging at a feast beforehand, he fights surprisingly well while still losing, and Gortwog names his newly won territory Orsinium.

books.title: Ice and Chiton
books.summary: Set during Tiber Septim's conquest of Tamriel in 2E 855, Commander Beatia of Ylliolos and her lieutenant Ascutus don brittle, ancient chitin armor found in a ruined keep to serve as a decoy while their four remaining guards escape across a frozen bay toward reinforcements at Gorvigh Ridge. The light armor lets the pair outrun pursuing Nord cavalry and leap onto rocky shore under arrow fire, and the collapsing ice drowns the pursuing horsemen behind them, allowing both officers to survive their sacrificial rearguard action.

books.title: Imperial Museum Welcome
books.summary: A brief welcome placard for the Imperial Museum and Library, signed by the Telvanni wizard Master Aryon, inviting visitors to view the exhibits but warning them to be cautious around a caged prisoner who has been in a foul mood since a failed escape attempt led to reduced rations.

books.title: Incident in Necrom
books.summary: A mercenary band hired by the Temple to cleanse a haunted cemetery near Necrom underestimates their illusionist teammate Massitha, who proves instrumental in paralyzing and blinding a nest of savage Quarra-clan vampires. After an ancient vampire ambushes the party and kills the leader Phlaxith, the surviving pair plot to abandon the wounded Massitha and keep her share of the reward, but she uses an invisibility spell to overhear their betrayal and steals the gold back from them.

books.title: Invocation of Azura
books.summary: A centuries-old priestess recounts her spiritual path through service to several Daedric Princes before finally devoting herself permanently to Azura. She describes leaving the manipulative cult of Molag Bal after her grandmother's death, the brutal and impersonal worship of Boethiah after accidentally killing her own brother in a ritual duel, and years spent trying to fathom the unknowable Nocturnal, before concluding that Azura alone values her worshippers' genuine emotional devotion rather than mere obedience.

books.title: Itermerel's Notes
books.summary: Fragmentary research notes by the scholar Itermerel on fluctuating 'Oblivion streams' of daedrons, which he claims affect a location's magicka potential, describing how manipulating magicka use and daedron field polarity can be used to trace and reconfigure these streams.

books.title: Jeleen's Sad Farewell
books.summary: A brief suicide note left by Jeleen, an Imperial Cult priest stationed at Fort Frostmoth, who declares he cannot go on living after losing his beloved Mirisa and intends to take his own life in hopes of reuniting with her, asking the Nine Divines for mercy on his soul.

books.title: Journal of Fryssa
books.summary: A brief, triumphant journal entry from an enchanter named Fryssa announces the completion of an enchanted robe called Whitewalker, which transforms its wearer into a snow-like form, and gloats defiantly about having been expelled from the Mages Guild over the project.

books.title: Journal of Tarhiel
books.summary: A brief, excited journal by the wizard Tarhiel documenting his development of an untested spell meant to let him leap vast distances through the air without the disorientation of standard levitation magic. Confident his calculations are complete, he declares he is ready to test it the next day and boasts of proving his mocking critics wrong, an experiment strongly implied to have gone fatally wrong.

books.title: Kagouti Mating Habits
books.summary: A naturalist's field notes on wild kagouti in southeastern Morrowind, observing that groups may only form larger packs near mating season, that females appear dominant in choosing mates while males offer food gifts and compete through vocalization rather than physical combat, and that all kagouti become notably more territorial and aggressive during the mating period.

books.title: Kagrenac's Journal
books.summary: An indecipherable journal attributed to the legendary Dwemer enchanter Kagrenac, written in an unfamiliar script and filled with complex numerical diagrams, with only its title page identifiable, in Aldmeris, as belonging to him.

books.title: Kagrenac's Planbook
books.summary: An untranslated Dwemer journal filled with complex diagrams and dense numeric annotations in an unknown script, identifiable only by its Ald Aldmeris title page as the personal planbook of the legendary Dwemer artificer Kagrenac.

books.title: Kagrenac's Tools
books.summary: A Dissident Priest account explains that the Dwemer priest Kagrenac forged three artifacts, Wraithguard, Sunder, and Keening, to safely draw on the divine power of Lorkhan's heart beneath Red Mountain, and that their use at the Battle of Red Mountain coincided with the Dwemer race's total disappearance. It recounts how Dagoth Ur, left to guard the recovered tools, secretly bonded himself to the heart's power and was driven mad, while Vivec, Almalexia, and Sotha Sil later broke their own oath, used the tools themselves to become gods, and were subtly corrupted in turn, an act the text frames as theft that dooms the Tribunal.

books.title: Last Scabbard of Akrash
books.summary: A veiled Dunmer woman secretly apprentices under a Tear armorer to learn sword-repair, later revealed to be Peliah, daughter of the slave-trading Houseman Dres Minegaur, who keeps her father's heirloom blade Akrash mysteriously pristine. She has actually been passing the sword nightly to her Khajiiti lover Kazagh, who uses it as the vigilante killer "the Lopper" to murder slave traders, including her arranged fiance. When a mortally wounded Kazagh comes to her window, her father discovers the affair, kills him with Akrash, and is in turn fatally stabbed by his own daughter with the same blade.

books.title: Legions of the Dead
books.summary: A reference overview categorizes Morrowind's undead into spirit revenants (ancestor ghosts, wraiths, dwarven ghosts) that require enchanted or silver weapons to harm, flesh revenants called bonewalkers that ordinary weapons can damage, and fleshless skeletal revenants of varying skill, with the powerful spirit-based bonelord as a dangerous exception. It further notes that vampires, once hunted to near extinction by the Ordinators and Buoyant Armigers, have recently reappeared in Morrowind, and clarifies that ash vampires are an unrelated, extremely dangerous phenomenon immune to typical anti-undead magic.

books.title: Letter from Gadayn
books.summary: A shopkeeper named Gadayn writes a clumsy, earnest love letter to a Wood Elf customer named Eraldil, whom he has admired silently every time she browsed his store, complimenting her appearance in awkward terms and offering her steep discounts in hopes of winning her affection.

books.title: Letter From J'Zhirr
books.summary: A promissory note issued by the East Empire Company, signed by an agent named J'Zhirr, pledging payment of ten thousand drakes to a recipient identified only by the initials 'LD' for unspecified services rendered, valid for one year or until paid in full.

books.title: Letter From Llaalam Dredil
books.summary: This brief business letter from someone signing as LD informs a partner referred to as J of newly agreed price increases across a range of goods, including minerals, textiles, paper, weapons, and armor, with by far the steepest hike reserved for a category labeled Artifacts. The clipped, transactional tone and unusually large markup on artifacts hints at a black-market or smuggling arrangement rather than ordinary commerce.

books.title: Letter from Ocato
books.summary: Imperial Chancellor Ocato issues a terse command to Arch-Mage Trebonius Artorius, ordering him to step down from active leadership of the Vvardenfell Mages Guild and transfer authority over Guild affairs to the recipient, while allowing him to retain the ceremonial title of Arch-Mage.

books.title: Letter from Rigmor to Risi
books.summary: In this personal letter, a man identified as RH pleads with a married woman named Risi to speak with him again, professes his love, criticizes her frequently absent husband, and hints that he may resort to drastic action if she continues to refuse him.

books.title: Letter to Senilias Cadiusus
books.summary: A brief letter of introduction from Hasphat Antabolis recommending the bearer to his acquaintance Senilias Cadiusus, citing their reliable service in retrieving an item from the Dwemer ruin of Arkngthand and asking that Cadiusus find them a place if possible.

books.title: Lives of the Saints
books.summary: A Tribunal Temple catechism lists the Dunmer Living Saints and the virtue each embodies: St. Nerevar the Captain for valor, martyred leading the Dunmer against the Dwemer and House Dagoth at Red Mountain; St. Veloth the Pilgrim for daring, who led the exodus from Summerset and taught the difference between Good and Bad Daedra; and further saints of generosity, mercy, justice, benevolence, and reverence, including Rilms, Aralor, Seryn, Felms, Roris, Olms, Delyn, Meris, and Llothis, each linked to a patron craft and a formative legend.

books.title: Lord Jornibret's Last Dance
books.summary: This traditional call-and-response ballad, sung alternately by women's and men's choruses, tells of Lord Ogin Jornibret, a nobleman notorious at the Queen of Rimmen's winter balls for cursing any maiden who dances with him. At one such ball he selects a woman he intends to seduce and abandon, praising her unexpected grace despite wearing hide armor, but the final verse reveals his intended victim had disguised herself in armor for self-protection, implying his scheme backfires. As poetry, only its subject, form, and comic-cautionary tone are described here, per the restriction against quoting verse.

books.title: Mages Guild Charter
books.summary: This Imperial charter establishes the Guild of Mages' mission to collect and share magical knowledge for the benefit of all Tamriel, founded on Summerset Isle by Vanus Galerion and Rilis XII and later reaffirmed under Potentate Versidue-Shaie. It sets membership requirements around mastery of Destruction, Alteration, Illusion, and Mysticism plus practical alchemy and enchanting knowledge, establishes strict internal discipline for crimes against fellow members, and lists the Guild's chapter halls across Vvardenfell in Ald'ruhn, Balmora, Caldera, Sadrith Mora, and Vivec.

books.title: Master Zoaraym's Tale
books.summary: Master Zoaraym tells his student Gi'Nanth how, decades earlier at the Temple of Two-Moons Dance in Torval, he was humbled during a graduation tournament by Taren Omathan, a quiet Dunmer servant who had secretly mastered hand-to-hand combat simply by observing students for years while cleaning the training halls. Taren then departs the temple to rejoin the struggles of his people in Morrowind, leaving Zoaraym with a lasting lesson in humility that he now passes on to his own pupils.

books.title: Message from Dagoth Ur
books.summary: In this letter addressed to Nerevar, Dagoth Ur recalls their former brotherhood and accuses Nerevar of striking him down at Red Mountain while he guarded treasures Nerevar had sworn him to protect. He reveals that the Sixth House was never destroyed, only dormant, and is now awakening to drive out Morrowind's foreign rulers and false gods, inviting Nerevar to Red Mountain to renew their friendship and share in his power.

books.title: Message from Master Aryon
books.summary: An unbroken coded message attributed to the Telvanni wizard-lord Master Aryon, written entirely in an indecipherable cipher script with no accompanying key. Its encryption suggests it conveys sensitive House Telvanni business meant to be read only by an intended recipient possessing the cipher.

books.title: Mission to Vivec -- from Caius
books.summary: Field notes from spymaster Caius Cosades instructing the reader to contact three informants in Vivec City -- Addhiranirr, a Khajiit Thieves Guild operative in St. Olms; Huleeya, an Argonian Morag Tong assassin at the Black Shalk Cornerclub; and Mehra Milo, a Temple priestess at the Hall of Wisdom and Justice -- to gather what each knows about the Nerevarine cult and the Sixth House cult, with a caution to protect Mehra Milo's secrecy.

books.title: Mixed Unit Tactics v1
books.summary: A Legion officer stationed at Fort Sphinxmoth recounts a battle from the Five Years War between the Khajiit and the Bosmer of Valenwood, describing how Khajiit tree-cutting teams lured Bosmer archers into the forest before Senche-raht shield-bearers pinned them down, ambushing Ohmes-raht ground troops emerged from hidden tunnels, and stealthy tree-dwelling Dagi-raht used magical silence and fire from the high branches to annihilate an entire company of archers for minimal Khajiit losses.

books.title: Mysterious Akavir
books.summary: An overview of Akavir's four rival nations: the demonic Kamal, who invade the monkey-folk of Tang Mo each summer; the immortal serpent-people of Tsaesci, who once consumed Akavir's human population and ruled the Cyrodilic Empire for centuries through Potentate Versidue-Shaie before his assassination; and the tiger-folk empire of Ka Po' Tun, now led by the dragon-emperor Tosh Raka, who intends to wipe out the Tsaesci and then invade Tamriel.

books.title: Mystery of Talara, Part 1
books.summary: During a millennial festival in the Breton city of Camlorn, a prostitute named Gyna is uncannily mistaken for a young noblewoman, first by the King and then by an old nurse who insists she recognizes a princess believed dead. Lady Jyllia reveals that the entire royal family, including a Princess Talara, was assassinated decades earlier. That night, during the Flower Festival, Gyna is pushed from a cliff by an unseen assailant, and clinging to the rock face she recovers a buried childhood memory of a wise king and a golden-haired girl teaching her how to fall safely, hinting she is the supposedly dead princess.

books.title: Mystery of Talara, Part 2
books.summary: Having survived a near-fatal fall from Cavilstyr Rock during the Flower Festival, the woman publicly known as the courtesan Gyna washes ashore near Camlorn and is healed by Ramke, an old nursemaid who once served Lady Jyllia Raze, the King's daughter. Ramke reveals that Jyllia witnessed the massacre of the royal family as a child and never fully recovered her memory or mind, which is why her father never named her heir; Gyna then chooses the road back toward Camlorn instead of fleeing home to Daggerfall, and is intercepted by Lord Strale, the Emperor's ambassador who had hired her as a court entertainer.

books.title: Mystery of Talara, Part 3
books.summary: In Camlorn, the royal battlemage Lord Eryl grows suspicious of ambassador Lord Strale's secretive investigation into a woman named Gyna, who closely resembles the murdered Princess Talara. Strale and Gyna meet the Emperor's agent Lady Brisienna, who agrees to help only if they can produce a confession naming who ordered the assassination decades earlier and prove the matter worth Imperial attention. Riding home they are ambushed by Eryl's men, and after the loyal servant Gnorbooth is killed by Eryl's own errant fire spell, Strale overpowers and begins interrogating the battlemage about the former Duke of Oloine.

books.title: Mystery of Talara, Part 4
books.summary: Gyna, trained in illusion magic by the Imperial nightblade Proseccus, seduces and then magically paralyzes the cruel Prince Sylon of Camlorn to help Lord Strale expose royal crimes. An old letter reveals that Jagar Tharn's treachery was suspected years before his infamous betrayal of the Emperor, and the King and Queen of Camlorn are arrested for the murder of the previous royal family, just as a mysterious woman resembling the long-vanished Princess Talara arrives at court.

books.title: Mystery of Talara, Part 5
books.summary: In the concluding volume of this serial, Lord Strale exposes that the King of Camlorn secretly hired an assassin to murder his own brother, the King and Queen, and eliminate the young Princess Talara so he could seize the throne, then had the assassin killed to silence him. Piecing together testimony and the recovered memories of the amnesiac woman known as Gyna, Strale reveals that the real Princess Talara survived the attack by falling into a river and losing her memory, while the woman raised as her traumatized cousin Lady Jyllia was in fact the usurper king's own daughter, the two girls having been mistaken for each other due to their close resemblance.

books.title: Mysticism
books.summary: An essay by Tetronius Lor explaining why Mysticism is the least understood school of magic, grouping together disparate effects like Soul Trap and Telekinesis whose underlying power source remains debated among scholars as Aetherius, Daedric energy, or leftover magicka from other spells. It notes that the Psijic Order calls Mysticism "the Old Way" and argues that mastering it requires patiently recognizing shifting magical patterns rather than the systematic research used in other schools.

books.title: N'Gasta! Kvata! Kvakis!
books.summary: Framed as an authentic magical text in the tongue of the Sload, supposedly authored by the Second Era necromancer N'Gasta, the book is actually an elaborate in-joke: its garbled prose is not a spell or lore at all but a disguised newsletter blurb aimed at fans of frogs, complete with talk of print versus online editions and club activities. It offers no translatable narrative content, functioning purely as a piece of hidden authorial humor rather than genuine in-world lore.

books.title: Nchunak's Fire and Faith
books.summary: In this fragment of a translated Dwemer travel account, the narrator questions a local informant about the state of religious learning among the Dwemer he represents, and is told that only the colony of Kherakah still earnestly studies Kagrenac's teachings, valuing understanding of the self's relation to the Heart above any merely practical or arcane knowledge.

books.title: Neminda's Orders
books.summary: A coded message (written in a simple letter-substitution cipher) reporting that House Hlaalu is rumored to be opening Rethan Manor as a new stronghold, and that an informant named Llethri believes he has found evidence of illegal Hlaalu ebony shipments out of Caldera. The orders direct one agent to meet with Llethri and another to watch a figure named Rethan Athyn, while noting that influence with the Duke will be used to block Hlaalu's contracts if possible, revealing a rival faction's covert campaign against Hlaalu's ebony trade.

books.title: Nerevar at Red Mountain
books.summary: This Apographa account, drawn from Ashlander oral tradition, describes how Nerevar and the Dwemer king Dumac kept an uneasy peace until Dagoth Ur revealed that Dwemer priest Kagrenac was secretly using the Heart of Lorkhan to forge a new god, a claim Azura confirmed. After Nerevar and Dumac fell in single combat during the resulting war, Dagoth Ur recovered Kagrenac's tools, but Nerevar's own commanders - Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec - poisoned him during a ritual meant to summon Azura, secretly coveting the Heart's power for themselves. Azura cursed the murderers by turning the Chimer into the ash-skinned Dunmer as a permanent mark of their betrayal, and the three went on to use the stolen tools to make themselves gods while Dagoth Ur was driven off and presumed destroyed.

books.title: Nerevar Moon-and-Star
books.summary: An Ashlander legend describing how the war-leader Nerevar united the House People and Tribes under his Ring of the Ancestors to defeat the Dwemer and expel outlanders at Red Mountain, only to be murdered in secret afterward by power-hungry Great House khans who then proclaimed themselves gods and abandoned his promises to the Tribes. The legend prophesies Nerevar's eventual return, ring in hand, to overthrow the false gods and restore the old bond between the Dunmer and their ancestral spirits.

books.title: Nerevarine cult notes
books.summary: A Blades intelligence briefing on the outlawed Nerevarine cult, which holds that a reborn Nerevar will one day topple the Tribunal Temple and drive outlanders from Morrowind, in contrast to Temple doctrine that honors Nerevar merely as a departed saint. It presents the widely known prophecy called "The Stranger" in its obscure verse form, noting a scholarly link between its imagery and a legendary ring of Nerevar's, and reports that related prophecies — the Seven Curses and the Seven Visions — have been lost from Ashlander memory, possibly deliberately.

books.title: Night Falls On Sentinel
books.summary: In a Sentinel tavern, the Redguard woman Haballa hires the retired assassin Jomic, who boasts of once using precise strikes to the body's 'pain centers' with a club to secretly abduct and kill Prince Arthago, the sickly elder brother of King Lhotun, decades before during the era of the War of Betony. Haballa then reveals herself as the King's agent sent to find him, and turns Jomic's own technique against him as punishment in a nearby alley.

books.title: No-h's Picture Book of Wood
books.summary: An extremely short, whimsical children's picture book offers a simple, cheerful rhyme celebrating wood as a material, closing with a crude joke scrawled in the margin as a final punchline.

books.title: Note from a Glenmoril Witch
books.summary: The Glenmoril Witch Agnes writes to her coven sisters stationed on Solstheim, explaining that she has crafted a one-use 'Scroll of the Wolf Ender' as a backup to repeatedly performing their standard lycanthropy-curing ceremony, and reveals that she has hidden the scroll inside a hollow icicle in their cave, reachable only in raven form or with a levitation potion.

books.title: Note from Bakarak
books.summary: A criminal leader named Bakarak warns an associate, Moris, that their operation has been betrayed to a necromancer named Goris, whose undead raiders wiped out most of a hideout at Dralas, sparing only one survivor to bring word. Suspecting an informant in the ranks, Bakarak refuses to surrender disputed goods, orders Moris to evacuate, and sends a courier named Ursine with a key to a new rendezvous point.

books.title: Note from Berwen
books.summary: A supplier named Berwen writes to a customer confirming that a single bed has been ordered in from Sadrith Mora and should reach them soon, weather and raiders permitting, welcoming the recipient to their new home in Vos.

books.title: Note from Bugrol
books.summary: A frantic note from an Orc named Bugrol to an ally named Bashuk asks for urgent rescue, explaining he is hiding from armed locals who suspect him of a crime the two of them committed together, and offers vague, roundabout directions to his hiding place among the rocks and trees.

books.title: Note from Carnius
books.summary: A short instructional note, signed only "C.M.," directs the recipient to use enclosed scrolls to secretly seize control of Hroldar's wolves and use them to kill Hroldar himself, since he is illiterate and unaware of the plan, explaining only that Hroldar can no longer be trusted and that the sender prefers to have others take the risk.

books.title: Note from Irgola
books.summary: In this short note, a pawnbroker named Irgola tells an associate, Bashuk, that a final notice has been sent to a debtor named Valvius and that Bashuk should be ready to resume rough debt-collection work once Valvius responds.

books.title: Note from Nelos
books.summary: A brief, apologetic love letter in which a self-described rogue named Nelos begs forgiveness from a woman named Maurrie for past wrongs, expresses disbelief at his good fortune that she has sent for him again, and promises to come to her as soon as he can.

books.title: Note from Oritius Maro
books.summary: A secret note from a conspirator named Oritius warns fellow plotters that Emperor Uriel Septim may visit Vvardenfell in person, urging them to watch his movements closely and strike if the chance arises. It calls for recruiting more members bound by an oath to die restoring 'a strong man' to the Imperial throne, and instructs its reader to destroy the note after reading it.

books.title: note from the Archcanon
books.summary: A cautious, formal letter from Archcanon Tholer Saryoni's office to an outlander claiming to be the Nerevarine, noting that Temple inquisitors have identified the claimant as an Imperial Blades agent, which deepens the Temple's suspicion of the prophecy claims. Saryoni states that a meeting is pointless unless the claimant first secures both titles -- Hortator from the three Great Houses and Nerevarine from all four Ashlander tribes -- and that he should then arrange a secure, discreet audience through the healer Danso Indules at the High Fane.

books.title: Note to Ahnia
books.summary: A frustrated seller writes to a woman named Ahnia explaining that an unspecified book has failed to sell, speculating that its poor reception is because too few people can actually read it, and warns that unless it moves soon, they intend to hand the unsold stock back to her rather than risk drawing further suspicion by holding onto it.

books.title: Note to Amaya
books.summary: A hurried note from Mehra to her friend Amaya, explaining she has gone to deliver documents to an Inquisitor at the Ministry of Truth and asking Amaya to meet her there, bringing along or replacing two borrowed Divine Intervention scrolls. A postscript notes Mehra has left behind Levitate potions in case Amaya cannot cast the spell herself.

books.title: Note to Falanaamo
books.summary: A casual note from a tavern patron named Shenk asking his friend Falanaamo to send him an order of netch leather shoes, inviting him for a free drink at a tavern called the Shovel, and jokingly asking him to share more about his past on Summerset Isle while sober this time.

books.title: Note to Giden
books.summary: A short note from a group leader named Rels instructs a subordinate, Giden, to arm a new recruit and assign him to sentry duty in place of an ill companion, while warning that bounty hunters are searching for their hideout.

books.title: Note to Hlevala
books.summary: Plantation owner Orvas Dren writes to his foreman Hlevala, praising the harsh disciplinary treatment imposed on enslaved Dunmer workers referred to dismissively as "nemer," and requests confirmation that several named individuals are accounted for so they can be formally registered as his property.

books.title: Note to Inorra
books.summary: A superior named Elyneaox disciplines a subordinate, Inorra, assigning her a full week of deep mine-scouting duty as punishment for an unspecified prior incident, with a pointed reminder about properly covering herself when outside afterward.

books.title: Note to Mages
books.summary: A brief safety memo from a supervisor named Stlennius warning mages guarding slaves in a mine to use fire spells cautiously, since flammable underground gases caused an explosive accident the previous week that injured a slave named Keseena.

books.title: Note to Salyn Sarethi
books.summary: A note from the vigilante group Bal Molagmer informs Serjo Salyn Sarethi that a blade called Enamor, stolen from him by one of their thieves, is being returned with an apology, since although they admired the theft's audacity, they judged Sarethi an unworthy target for it.

books.title: Note to Slaves
books.summary: A posted set of harsh mine-camp regulations for slaves, forbidding damage to bedposts, talking after sundown, during feedings, or before sunrise, and demanding immediate, unquestioning obedience to guards and mages.

books.title: Note to Valvius
books.summary: A pawnbroker named Irgola writes to a customer, Valvius, refusing to fill a new order of Cyrodilic Brandy until an overdue balance from a previous shipment is settled, and warns that continued delay could bring unwanted attention from local enforcers.

books.title: Notes from Huleeya
books.summary: A spy's briefing notes for Caius Cosades explain that Ashlander tribes were economically and politically sidelined once Temple-backed Great Houses grew dominant, fueling their reverence for the Nerevarine prophecy as a promise to restore the vanished equality of Nerevar's Peace. It relays the Ashlander oral account of Nerevar's oath on the Ring of the Ancestors, his betrayal and murder by House khans who then styled themselves gods, and the foretold return of an Incarnate to fulfill his old promises. It also describes the Tribunal Temple's persecution of Nerevarine claimants, mentions a recent false claimant known as Peakstar, and notes the Ashlander belief in a Cavern of the Incarnates holding the spirits of past failed claimants.

books.title: Notes on Racial Phylogeny
books.summary: A scholarly survey from the Imperial University's healers on interfertility among Tamriel's peoples, concluding that men and mer readily interbreed with fertile offspring while claims of children between them and Khajiit or Argonians remain unverified. It weighs where Argonians fit relative to the dreugh and other lizardfolk, admits the reproductive biology of orcs, goblins, and daedra is largely unstudied, and confirms that the hermaphroditic sload of Thras cannot interbreed with men or mer.

books.title: NoteToCalderaGuard
books.summary: A short instruction from an official named Elynea directing Caldera's guards to closely watch an Argonian called "Gold-Heart," who has grown increasingly defiant toward authority, particularly around Argonian women.

books.title: Odral's History of the Empire 1
books.summary: This chronicle traces the Septim line from Tiber Septim's conquest that founded the Third Era through the short, murdered reign of Pelagius I, the prosperous rule of Kintyra I, the lawmaking of Uriel I, the troubled years of Uriel II, and the corrupt but stabilizing reign of Pelagius II and flamboyant Antiochus. It ends on the tragedy of Antiochus's daughter Kintyra II, overthrown and eventually killed in prison after her cousin Uriel III seized the throne with the backing of Potema of Solitude, setting up the War of the Red Diamond as the next volume's subject.

books.title: Odral's History of the Empire 3
books.summary: This third volume of an Imperial history covers the reigns from Uriel IV through Uriel V. It details how Uriel IV, adopted rather than born into the Septim line, struggled against a defiant Elder Council that later disinherited his son Andorak in favor of Cephorus II; how Cephorus II's reign was overshadowed by the Camoran Usurper's daedra-and-undead rampage through Valenwood and Hammerfell; and how Uriel V restored Imperial military prestige through conquests of Roscrea, Cathnoquey, Yneslea, and Esroniet before dying in a failed invasion of Akavir at the Battle of Ionith.

books.title: Odral's History of the Empire 4
books.summary: This fourth installment of Stronach k'Thojj III's imperial history covers Uriel VI's decades-long struggle to wrest real power from the Elder Council and his mother's regency, his sister Morihatha's deliberate but successful reconquest campaigns before her assassination in 3E339, and Pelagius IV's 49-year reign restoring imperial unity. It concludes with Uriel Septim VII's reign, his betrayal and ten-year imprisonment by his Imperial Battlemage Jagar Tharn, and his eventual rescue in 3E399 by an unnamed Champion.

books.title: Odral's Land Deed
books.summary: A land sale deed formally sealed under the Tribunal's authority, recording two property transfers by Rovone Arvel: a tract bordering Arvel Manor purchased by Orvas Dren, and a nearby smallholding near Fort Pelagiad bought separately by Odral Helvi, with signatures from buyers and seller alike.

books.title: Old Dwemer Book
books.summary: An untranslated Dwemer-language manual, identifiable from its diagrams as a technical guide covering combustibles and fire safety procedures.

books.title: Old Dwemer Book
books.summary: An untranslated Dwemer text whose accompanying schematics indicate it is a technical manual covering the replacement and maintenance of mechanical cogs.

books.title: Old Dwemer Book
books.summary: This book is written entirely in an untranslated Dwemer script and appears, based on its accompanying schematics, to be a technical manual covering the maintenance of Dwemer machinery.

books.title: Old Dwemer Book
books.summary: A text written in an untranslated Dwemer language, accompanied by technical schematics, that appears from its diagrams to be a manual on the fabrication of metals, offering an unreadable but tantalizing glimpse of lost Dwemer metallurgical craft.

books.title: Old Dwemer Book
books.summary: Written entirely in an untranslated Dwemer script, this volume's diagrams suggest it is a technical instruction manual covering methods for fitting and joining pipe, likely tied to the maintenance of Dwemer plumbing or machinery.

books.title: Old Dwemer Book
books.summary: This book is written in an unrecognized Dwemer language and, based on its accompanying schematics, appears to be a technical manual describing how Dwemer machines regulate or consume power, though its untranslated contents are otherwise inaccessible to the reader.

books.title: Old Dwemer Book
books.summary: An untranslated text written in a Dwemer language, whose accompanying diagrams suggest it is a technical manual on channeling water and managing pressure, offering a glimpse of Dwemer engineering without any content a reader can otherwise interpret.

books.title: Old, Wet Note
books.summary: Heinlen the Heavy writes to Winter-Fist warning that a rival named Angria and her group tried to steal ancient armor once belonging to the Snow Prince, kept within Jolgierr Barrow; though driven off, the thieves escaped with the helmet and are believed to be hiding near Lake Fjalding or the Frykte ice cave.

books.title: On Morrowind
books.summary: This historical essay explains how Morrowind avoided ruinous conquest during Tiber Septim's expansion when Vivec personally negotiated a secret treaty preserving Dunmer self-rule and religious autonomy in exchange for provincial status, a deal whose exact terms and circumstances were never recorded. It details how the Great Houses split over resistance, with Indoril and Dres favoring defiance to the death, Hlaalu favoring accommodation, Redoran privately relieved, and Telvanni opportunistically siding with the winners, and notes that more Dunmer blood was ultimately spilled in the internal power struggle following the assassination of the resisting Lord High Councilor than in any fighting against the Legions.

books.title: On Oblivion
books.summary: Scholar Morian Zenas surveys written and testimonial evidence about Oblivion and its ruling Daedra princes, correcting the common but inaccurate use of the term demon and listing figures such as Sanguine, Boethiah, Molag Bal, Sheogorath, Azura, Mephala, Malacath, and Namira among others. He groups Mehrunes Dagon, Molag Bal, Peryite, Boethiah, and Vaernima as the most destructively inclined princes and briefly characterizes how each expresses that destructiveness. He closes by naming his next research goals: the elusive prince Hircine and a practical method for mortals to travel physically into Oblivion.

books.title: Order From Mollismo
books.summary: A brief work order from the Telvanni steward Mollismo instructs the servant Galen to deliver two crates of steel armor to the tower by nightfall on the orders of the wizard-lord Therana, warning that her temper has grown short amid rumors of an impending siege by a rival named Trerayna.

books.title: Orders for Bivale Teneran
books.summary: A document addressed as orders for a person named Bivale Teneran, but rendered in scrambled or corrupted text that cannot be deciphered into any coherent message, leaving its actual instructions or intent unknown.

books.title: Ordo Legionis
books.summary: Outlines the Imperial Legion's role maintaining order in Vvardenfell District through five garrisons, naming Moonmoth, Buckmoth, and Fort Pelagiad as full-strength town garrisons, Hawkmoth as an elite honor guard, and Fort Darius as the sole undermanned frontier post. It lays out the combat skills and physical standards expected of recruits, including proficiency with long blade, spear, and blunt weapons, defense using heavy armor, and stamina for marching and maneuvering.

books.title: Origin of the Mages Guild
books.summary: Written by Archmage Salarth, this history describes how the Psijic mage Vanus Galerion broke from the secretive, aristocratic tradition of magic to found the Mages Guild in Firsthold, offering spells and magical goods to any paying member of the public despite Psijic and royal suspicion. It traces the Guild's early security troubles (leading to the Order of the Lamp), its spread across Tamriel, its six-Archmagister governing structure, and Galerion's own later, bitter verdict that his creation had become mired in political infighting.

books.title: Overview of Gods and Worship
books.summary: Brother Hetchfeld's essay wrestles with why the gods of Tamriel seem to intervene generously for some favored mortals through blessings and artifacts, yet appear indifferent through famines and plagues. He proposes that deities may draw their strength from worship and pious deeds, and speculates that some lesser spirits encountered in the world could be the diminished remnants of gods who lost their followers, possibly even capable of rising again toward divinity.

books.title: Package for Caius Cosades
books.summary: A sealed courier package addressed to the Blades agent Caius Cosades, written entirely in an unbroken substitution cipher that cannot be read without the appropriate key. Its encrypted form marks it as a covert intelligence dispatch tied to the Emperor's secret operations in Morrowind, though its actual contents remain inaccessible without decoding.

books.title: Palla, Book I
books.summary: A young Mages Guild initiate at the backwater Mir Corrup chapter recounts investigating a confiscated necromantic artifact and then attending a holiday ball hosted by a reclusive young Redguard heiress, Betaniqi, newly arrived from Hammerfell. At the ball he becomes consumed by obsession after helping unveil a statue of Betaniqi's late mother, Palla, a renowned warrior famed for slaying a monstrous beast at the cost of her own life, and the volume ends with the narrator's mind and dreams entirely given over to the image of her.

books.title: Palla, Book II
books.summary: A Mages Guild initiate becomes obsessively infatuated with the statue of a deceased Redguard warrior-woman named Palla, memorialized by her grieving daughter Betaniqi, and switches his studies to Enchantment under Magister Ilther in hopes of powering a stolen necromantic disc he believes can revive her. Months of secret nighttime practice bring him no closer, and the disc shatters in a storm just before he confesses his obsession to Betaniqi. She reveals in horror that her mother's name was actually Xarlys, and that "Palla" was the name of the monster her mother died killing, which he then encounters waiting for him on the road.

books.title: Parchment with Scrawlings
books.summary: A deranged, ecstatic scrawled rant proclaiming the awakening of a singular, all-powerful being who claims dominion over names, shadows, and celestial bodies, framed as an apocalyptic revelation of a returning godlike 'Lord.' The feverish, cultic tone strongly evokes Sixth House fervor surrounding the stirring of Dagoth Ur.

books.title: Peke Utchoo's last words
books.summary: An adventurer named Peke Utchoo scrawls a final, wryly humorous note after surviving a fight with a Dwemer centurion inside a flooded ruin, only to grab the wrong bottle in the dark and swallow poison instead of a healing draught. Dying and resigned to his fate, he leaves behind a key found near the entrance, jokes about his terrible luck, and warns whoever finds him not to make the same mistake with the leftover bottle.

books.title: Plan to Defeat Dagoth Ur
books.summary: Signed by Vivec on the Tribunal's behalf, this strategy document lays out a five-stage campaign for the Nerevarine: scout the Ghostfence interior, hunt down Dagoth Ur's ash-vampire kin, then storm the citadels holding Dagoth Vemyn and Dagoth Odros to reclaim the artifacts Sunder and Keening, before finally striking Dagoth Ur himself using Wraithguard, Sunder, and Keening together. It explains that these Dwemer tools once let the Tribunal tap the Heart of Lorkhan for godhood, and that striking the Heart with Keening a second time should permanently unravel that connection for everyone bound to it, ending both Dagoth Ur's power and possibly the Tribunal's own divinity. It closes with warnings that Wraithguard is mandatory protection around the other two relics and that Dagoth Ur will likely try to bargain with or corrupt the Nerevarine.

books.title: Poison Song I
books.summary: Young Tay, an orphaned ward of House Indoril raised on the island of Gorne, is privately tormented by a strange, wordless music only he can hear and by recurring dream-visions no one else believes. Exploring a hidden, wreckage-strewn gorge with his cousins Baynarah and the younger Vaster, Tay becomes obsessed with a glowing crystal orb Vaster digs from a ruined wagon. Driven by the swelling music, Tay lets Vaster fall to his death over the cliff edge and secretly keeps the orb, lying to Baynarah about what happened.

books.title: Poison Song II
books.summary: A boy named Tay realizes, without guilt, that he murdered his young cousin Vaster to obtain a mysterious crystal globe tied to a haunting psychic "Song," while the family fruitlessly searches the woods for the missing child. His devoted nursemaid Edebah, unknown to him, has been quietly guiding him toward the artifact and is later caught by his cousin Baynarah performing a candlelit ritual using symbols of the long-destroyed Sixth House of Dagoth. Baynarah discards relics they had found linked to House Dagoth and has Edebah banished, but keeps her suspicions from Tay out of fear of him.

books.title: Poison Song III
books.summary: As a young student in Mournhold, Tay falls for a fellow Temple initiate named Acra while receiving affectionate letters from his cousin Baynarah back on Gorne. He then encounters his estranged former nursemaid Edebah, who reveals he was actually adopted into House Indoril as a Sixth House orphan after the War of the Red Mountain and presses an ancestral ring on him; overwhelmed by the same murderous compulsion that once made him kill a cousin, Tay kills Edebah and sets her home ablaze.

books.title: Poison Song IV
books.summary: Tay confesses to his lover Acra that he has just killed his childhood nursemaid Edebah after she revealed he secretly descends from House Dagoth and bears its sealing ring, hearing an ancestral 'Song' that has compelled him to kill before. Acra reveals she too carries Dagoth blood and is in fact his sister, prompting Tay to murder another kinsman and flee into the wilderness, ultimately leaping from a cliff into the sea, only to wash up alive on a distant shore near his cousin Baynarah.

books.title: Poison Song V
books.summary: Recovering from a near-fatal ordeal, Tay confesses to his cousin Baynarah that he is secretly Dagoth-Tython, heir of the outlawed Sixth House, and that an ancestral compulsion he calls the Song has already driven him to kill his old nursemaid Edebah and two kinsmen. Baynarah refuses to accept it, but a Temple priestess arrives claiming to be his true sister Dagoth-Acra; after Tay flees, she and hidden accomplices massacre the household's servants and guards before escaping by a spell of Recall, having drawn Tay fully into the Sixth House's plans.

books.title: Poison Song VI
books.summary: This installment follows House caravan commander Jasrat, whose weapons shipment is ambushed by Dagoth rebels Tython and his sister Acra disguised as Ashlanders. Acra is then captured by House Indoril warrior Baynarah, who has infiltrated the rebels and tortures her for the location of a planned assassination of General Indoril-Triffith, only for Acra to escape before revealing Tython's exact whereabouts. The chapter portrays the Sixth House uprising as a guerrilla insurgency against House Indoril and the Temple, with Baynarah torn between duty and horror at the mounting bloodshed.

books.title: Poison Song VII
books.summary: At the Indoril fortress of Barysimayn near Red Mountain, General Triffith is confronted by his vengeful nephew Tython, who calls himself Dagoth-Tython and is driven by an inherited ancestral 'Song' to avenge his slain father. Tython's cousin Baynarah begs him to resist the Song's influence, but he escapes and hurls himself into the volcano's crater, after which the mysterious and now-pregnant Dagoth-Acra retrieves his House Dagoth ring and inherits the Song for herself.

books.title: Private Notes -- DO NOT READ
books.summary: This fragment amounts to little more than jumbled figures and unreadable marks, leaving no recoverable content beyond a signature identifying the owner as Elbert Nermarc.

books.title: Progress of Truth
books.summary: Compiled by the Dissident Priests, this tract lays out their formal challenges to Tribunal Temple orthodoxy, suggesting the Tribunal's divine power may derive from the same corrupted Dwemer devices that produced the false construct Numidium, and pointing to contradictions between the Temple's public teachings and its hidden Apographa writings. It notes that Ashlander tradition denies the Tribunal fought at Red Mountain and instead blames Nerevar's death on treachery at a council, and it condemns the Ordinators' use of torture and the persecution of believers in the Nerevarine prophecies while still honoring the Tribunal's sainthood.

books.title: Provinces of Tamriel
books.summary: A geographic and cultural survey of the nine provinces of the Tamrielic Empire, covering the warlike Nords of Skyrim, the maritime Redguards of Hammerfell, the independent clans of High Rock, the isolated high culture of Summerset Isle, the sparsely settled forests of Valenwood, the split between urban and nomadic Khajiit populations in Elsweyr, the swamp-dwelling Argonians of Black Marsh who have long suffered Dunmer slave raids, Morrowind's Great House-governed Dunmer homeland, and Cyrodiil's jungle-covered imperial heartland.

books.title: Public notice
books.summary: An official Temple and Ordinator proclamation denouncing the outlaw claiming the titles 'Incarnate' and 'Nerevarine' as a fraud secretly employed by Imperial Intelligence, declaring the associated prophecies discredited, and calling on citizens to report or raise the alarm if they spot the accused, issued under the authority of Grandmaster Berel Sala.

books.title: Realizations of Acrobacy
books.summary: An acrobatic troupe led by Rhunen Zebavi is invited to entertain the Telvanni wizard Gothren, who is locked in a rivalry with fellow councilor Neloth. Rhunen recounts how his troupe, after being wrongly suspected of spying and tortured by Neloth (which killed their Khajiit tumbler S'Rabba), took revenge by using extraordinary climbing, tumbling, and escape feats to steal Neloth's prized artifact, Mehrunes' Razor, from his tower. Gothren is delighted by the tale and welcomes the troupe as honored guests, though the story leaves the razor's ultimate fate untold.

books.title: Red Book of 3E 426
books.summary: This annual House Redoran register for 3E 426 names the six sitting Vvardenfell councilors, led by Archmaster Bolvyn Venim, along with their manor titles and territorial holdings around Ald'ruhn. It records the council's grievances over trade duties that favor imported flin at the expense of native drinks, growing violence tied to competition between the Thieves Guild and Camonna Tong, and a bloody tax revolt in Balmora that officials worried might spread.

books.title: Redoran Cooking Secrets
books.summary: A short collection of two traditional House Redoran recipes: a baked dish of crab meat, scuttle, and kwama egg, and a savory pie of mixed rat and hound meat with saltrice and ash salts, presented as household culinary tips.

books.title: Redoran Vaults Ledger
books.summary: This entry is framed as an internal House Redoran financial record, intended to track incoming and outgoing dealings and the current state of the house's treasury, though the excerpt itself provides no actual transaction figures or dates.

books.title: Reflections on Cult Worship
books.summary: In a letter written from the Vos Tradehouse, Imperial trader Cuseius Plecia contrasts Heartlander religious attitudes -- casual, abstract, and centered on figures like Akatosh, Dibella, and the Tiber Septim cult -- with the intensely personal Dunmer ancestor worship and Tribunal devotion, in which the Tribunal gods are believed to walk the earth and watch over daily life. He argues this difference in religious temperament underlies much of the cultural friction between the Empire and Morrowind.

books.title: Release Identification
books.summary: This is the player character's official release document from Imperial custody, issued by the Seyda Neen Census and Excise office under the Emperor's decree, recording the bearer's name, race, and class and formally admitting them into the district of Vvardenfell.

books.title: Rels Tenim Journal Page
books.summary: A journal entry describing how the writer's group struck a bargain with dangerous creatures nesting in a ruined tomb they discovered within their cave hideout, agreeing to lure bounty hunters and other intruders to their deaths as "sustenance" in exchange for continued safe refuge. The writer notes growing unease, shared by a companion named Mulvrulea, that the arrangement cannot end well.

books.title: Response from Divayth Fyr
books.summary: This scroll, attributed to the wizard-sage Divayth Fyr, consists entirely of an unbroken block of scrambled capital letters with no recognizable words or grammar, indicating an enciphered or otherwise encoded message that cannot be understood without whatever key or method was used to scramble it.

books.title: Response to Bero's Speech
books.summary: Battlemage Malviser rebuts a published speech by the illusionist Berevar Bero that attacked the School of Destruction as shallow, disputing Bero's historical claims about past Imperial Battlemages such as Zurin Arctus, Hethoth, Welloc, and Jagar Tharn. Malviser argues Destruction is a deep and subtle discipline in its own right, defends it against Bero's proposal to fold it into Alteration, and suggests Bero's own background in Illusion has biased his critique.

books.title: Rethan Manor Land Deed
books.summary: A legal deed recording the sale of Rethan Manor, on the northeast coast of the River Odai south of Balmora, to a member of House Hlaalu, sealed by the House's treasurer Baren Alen as seller and witnessed under the authority of ALMSIVI.

books.title: Rogue Necromancer's Journal
books.summary: In this journal, an unrepentant necromancer complains about societal restrictions on his practice and describes struggling to control savage, ice-protected draugr on Solstheim, in contrast to the easier corpses he found on Vvardenfell. He notes that his apprentices are growing more powerful and excitedly records having located the Mantle of Woe within the Rimhull ice cave, which he intends to claim for himself.

books.title: Royal Writ of Execution
books.summary: Issued under the royal authority of King Hlaalu Helseth, this writ designates Bedal Alen as condemned, empowering its bearer to carry out the killing as a legally sanctioned royal execution.

books.title: Royal Writ of Execution
books.summary: An official writ, issued in the name of King Hlaalu Helseth, authorizing whoever carries it to kill a man named Forven Berano on sight, granting the bearer legal immunity for carrying out the execution.

books.title: Royal Writ of Execution
books.summary: A brief royal writ issued under the authority of King Hlaalu Helseth, granting its bearer official sanction to kill the named outlaw Hloggar the Bloody.

books.title: Saint Nerevar
books.summary: Written as a Temple primer for outsiders, this short pamphlet summarizes the life of Saint Nerevar, the Dunmer general who used the Ring of the Ancestors to unite the Great Houses against the Dwemer and the traitorous House Dagoth at Red Mountain. Though he ultimately died of wounds dealt by Dagoth Ur himself, Nerevar lived long enough to witness the Temple's founding, and is now venerated among its communion of saints.

books.title: Saryoni's Sermons
books.summary: A widely circulated Tribunal Temple devotional compiled by Archcanon Tholer Saryoni, gathering Vivec's teachings into short maxims about faith and the redemptive value of suffering, followed by the formal litany of the Seven Graces -- Valor, Daring, Justice, Courtesy, Pride, Generosity, and Humility -- each rendered as a brief vow of devotion meant to be recited by the faithful.

books.title: Saryoni's Sermons Manuscript
books.summary: Presented as the source manuscript behind Archcanon Tholer Saryoni's public sermons, this text gives five short maxims attributed to Vivec on faith and enduring suffering, followed by the Temple's Seven Graces, Valor, Daring, Justice, Courtesy, Pride, Generosity, and Humility, each phrased as a brief devotional statement of the virtue expected of a faithful worshipper.

books.title: Scroll of Daerir's Blessing
books.summary: A short ritual invocation calling on a water-associated figure named Daerir to cleanse the reciter of a corrupting affliction, using imagery of storms and deep waters. Composed as a rhythmic, incantatory blessing rather than a narrative, its tone is solemn and purifying, consistent with a prayer meant to counter blight-borne sickness.

books.title: Scroll of Daerir's Miracle
books.summary: A ritual invocation scroll, written as verse, that calls on a primordial water-dwelling entity for cleansing power against the corrupting red ash of Morrowind's volcanic land. Its tone is solemn and incantatory, structured as a set of parallel calls followed by a personal vow of purification.

books.title: Scroll of Elemental Burst:Fire
books.summary: A formal Morag Tong writ of execution naming an individual condemned to "honorable execution" under Morag Tong law, and certifying its bearer as officially sanctioned to carry out the killing.

books.title: Scroll of Tyronius
books.summary: A dying tomb raider named Tyronius writes a final letter to his brother, describing how his party was overwhelmed by undead that seemed to materialize from nowhere inside a tomb they believed was cleared, killing two of his companions, Jonis and Luven. Trapped in the burial chamber with payment owed to him by a man named Goris for completed work, Tyronius asks his brother to find Goris in his own tomb-lair in Tel Mora, using a forged key, and avenge the betrayal.

books.title: Secret Caldera Ledger
books.summary: A mining record book tracking ebony shipments out of the Caldera mines shows a consistent diversion of proceeds into something labeled the 'Ashlands Management Fund,' suggesting that someone with access to the mine's output is quietly siphoning wealth toward an undisclosed personal project.

books.title: Senilius' Report
books.summary: Dwemer ruin excavator Senilius Cadiusus writes to his patron Edwinna about slow progress at Nchuleftingth, explaining that deep, still-functioning Dwemer machinery remains out of reach without the lost knowledge of the Passwall scrolls. He clarifies that "Mzuleft" is the correct name for a separate set of ruins south of Dagon Fel, reports dismantling the site's last active centurion spider, and relays a ship captain's account of a captured centurion that inexplicably stopped functioning once carried away from Vvardenfell's waters, only reactivating when the ship turned back.

books.title: Settler's Journal
books.summary: A short journal from a Solstheim settler describing the discovery and claiming of an ice cave called Legge, previously inhabited by bears and wolves, as a new home for the family. Later entries note ongoing trouble with a persistent bear that steals food, with the settler relying on an inherited enchanted ring to keep the local wildlife at bay.

books.title: Sharn's Legions of the Dead
books.summary: A bestiary of Morrowind's undead distinguishing spirit revenants such as ancestor ghosts, wraiths, and dwarven ghosts, which require enchanted or silver weapons to harm, from flesh-based bonewalkers, which ordinary weapons can damage, and skeletal fleshless revenants whose combat skill mirrors their former life, with the rare bonelord singled out as an especially dangerous exception requiring enchanted weapons. It also notes that vampires were nearly wiped out in Morrowind by Ordinators and Buoyant Armigers but have recently reappeared, and clarifies that so-called ash vampires are an entirely different, extremely dangerous phenomenon immune to standard anti-undead magic.

books.title: Shipping Notice
books.summary: A mundane shipping log recording routine deliveries of everyday goods such as drink, food, and furniture to the Varo Tradehouse, with one entry noting a recent delivery of several crates of cheese.

books.title: Shishi Report
books.summary: A brief battle report informs an unnamed superior that a five-person party has captured the Velothi tower of Shishi from five Telvanni sorcerers at heavy cost, and that the sender intends to hold the position while awaiting further orders.

books.title: Silence
books.summary: Before confronting the rogue battlemage Egroamaro in the Grazelands, the adventurer Oristian Silverthorn pays a retired Illusion teacher, Erer Darothil, to teach him the Silence spell instead of invisibility or darkness, wanting to master only one technique before returning to his worried wife. He uses it to mute Egroamaro's incantations and kill him with ease, then returns home to Gnisis, where the story closes with him quietly using the same spell to tune out his nagging wife Liah.

books.title: Sithis
books.summary: This Sixth House scripture recasts Sithis as the primal force of chaotic nothingness from which all possibility springs, opposed by the 'false god' Anui-El and the Aedra he gathers around him, who are portrayed as enslaving Sithis's fleeting ideas into static, imperfect realms. It identifies Lorkhan as Sithis's agent sent to unravel the Aedric order from within by posing as a friend, ending with an invocation urging the reader to approach Dagoth Ur, called the Sharmat, in the same guise of friendship.

books.title: Smuggler's Island
books.summary: After a storm sinks their moon sugar smuggling run, Harithoel and the injured S'Riizh wash up on a barren island with no fresh water or food, and Harithoel teaches himself to fish with an improvised spear to keep them both alive for nearly two months. When a rescue ship finally arrives, S'Riizh suddenly reveals he can walk after all and had secretly been studying Harithoel's spear technique, then kills him with his own weapon so as not to have to split the smuggled cargo's profits.

books.title: Song of the Alchemists
books.summary: Part of the comic "Ancient Tales of the Dwemer" series attributed to Marobar Sul, this rhyming poem describes a Dwemer king staging a contest between two rival alchemists to see who can brew a potion of invisibility for him. One competitor succeeds while the other unwittingly brews a potion of intelligence due to a mix-up in reading ingredient colors under colored light, and a publisher's note frames the piece as broad, anti-intellectual humor from the Interregnum period rather than an authentic account of Dwemer belief.

books.title: Sottilde's Code Book
books.summary: A short passage of text attributed to a person named Sottilde, written entirely in a substitution cipher rather than plain language. Its enciphered form implies a private or secretive record, though the content itself cannot be determined without the corresponding cipher key.

books.title: Sovngarde, a Reexamination
books.summary: This essay examines the Nord legend of Sovngarde, the hidden hall built by the god Shor to reward warriors who fall valiantly in combat, and the long, largely fruitless tradition of Nords searching for its physical entrance. It presents newly discovered correspondence between a medium named Felga Four-Fingers and the ghost of a slain warrior, Rolf the Large, as evidence that death itself in honorable battle, rather than any hidden location, is the true gateway into Shor's hall.

books.title: Special Flora of Tamriel
books.summary: A herbalist's catalog of unusual Tamrielic plants -- including Poppy, Fire Fern, Dragon's Tongue, Domica Redwort, Ironwood Nut, Ginko leaves, Somnalius Fern, Arrowroot, and Nightshade -- noting where each grows and the magical or alchemical effects folk tradition attributes to them, from fire resistance and levitation to enhanced stealth and stamina.

books.title: Spirit of Nirn, God of Mortals
books.summary: A short theological essay on Lorkhan as the Spirit of Nirn, contrasting the Elves who resent him as the being who severed them from the spirit realm with the Men who revere him as the herald of existence. It lays out two competing views of the created world: an illusory prison to be escaped back to the spirit realm, or a necessary testing ground toward genuine transcendence.

books.title: Spirit of the Daedra
books.summary: A Dremora-authored text explains daedric psychology to mortals: Daedra do not truly die, since a destroyed body's spirit simply returns from the Darkness, though lesser Scamps and Vermai feel little or no fear while Dremora must actively master it. It describes daedric clan and oath-bonds to greater masters such as Mehrunes Dagon, and frames mortals as prey hunted for sport, expressing genuine daedric bafflement at why humans, doomed to permanent death, do not despair.

books.title: Starlover's Log
books.summary: The final journal entries of Battlemage Samar Starlover, chronicling the desperate last stand of the Battlespire against an overwhelming Daedric assault tied to Mehrunes Dagon. Starlover recounts his failed final gambit of flying his dragon companion, Dragonne Papre, toward the Imperial Palace for reinforcements after the Weir Gate is lost, only to find the main gate sealed against retreat, and he accepts death asking that his sister be told of his fate.

books.title: Surfeit of Thieves
books.summary: Thieves Indyk and Heriah target the ruined castle Ald Olyra after learning that a reclusive group calling itself the Order of St. Eadnua is holding a lavish feast there.
